  lifecycle step lands in the receipt trail
  (`<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/receipts.jsonl`, `ScheduledReceiptLog`,
  best-effort): scheduled / delivered / delivery_failed / scan_failed
  (queue) and wake_attempted / turn_started / wake_refused (both hosts'
  wake paths; refusal receipts are once per refusal EPISODE — the latch
  lives in `InboxWakePolicy` next to the streak, so a held gate cannot
  spam the trail and a repeat episode after user input is receipted
  again).
  Sleep resilience (issue #259): all due math rides an injectable wall
  clock (`ScheduledMessageQueue(clock:)`), long waits are split into ≤60s
  timer legs (`maxTimerLeg`) that recompute the remaining delay from the
  wall clock on every fire — never accumulating duration drift — and
  hosts run a catch-up sweep at every TURN START (CLI `_beginUserPrompt`,
  app `sendText`) in addition to the idle inbox ticks, so the first
  post-sleep turn delivers every overdue record immediately. Catch-up is
  exactly-once per record (file removed on send + the `_delivering`
  in-flight guard) — missed cycles of a recurring self-re-arm are NOT
  replayed; the re-armed cycle simply resumes from "now". For true
  sleep-proofing (delivery DURING lid sleep) no in-process timer can
  help: add an external pinger, e.g. a cron/launchd entry that messages
  the session's mailbox — mail to an asleep session already launches a
  headless wake run that drains the inbox and sweeps due records.
 Failure isolation (issue #270): a throwing `send` is contained per
 record (logged via `onError` — CLI `[sched]` line, app `AppLog`), the
 record stays for the next sweep, and the post-failure re-arm floors the
 leg at `failureBackoff` (60s) so a poison record cannot spin a
 zero-delay timer; sweeps deliver in due-time order, and the app's
 turn-start sweep is awaited so the fresh turn sees the fired reminder.
 A failed SCAN (transient `listDir`/read error on a leg, gh-1180) is
 equally loud: `onError` + a `scan_failed` receipt, then a re-arm at
 `failureBackoff` — the arming heartbeat never silently disarms
 ("scan failed" used to be treated as "nothing pending", permanently
 disarming the scheduler with zero log). Corrupt record CONTENT is
 still skipped, not fatal (issue #59). Every lifecycle step is
 receipted to an append-only JSONL trail at
 `<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/receipts.jsonl` (`ScheduledReceiptLog`,
 gh-1180): `scheduled` / `delivered` (with lag) / `delivery_failed` /
 `scan_failed` from the queue, plus host-side `wake_attempted` /
 `turn_started` / `wake_refused` (with reason) from the CLI wake path —
 a post-mortem can distinguish "timer never fired" (no `delivered`)
 from "wake refused" without reading source. The trail is best-effort:
 a failing write logs via `onError` and never breaks scheduling.
 Records carry the scheduling instance's `owner` (mailbox prefix): a
 sweeper re-addresses a self-addressed record only when the stored owner
 matches its own prefix, and never deletes another instance's record -
 foreign-owned records are left where their owner sweeps (also across a
 root change: only own records migrate to an adopted folder's root).
 Legacy untagged records drain via the old any-sweeper path; records
 whose owner session is deleted (`/reset` mints a new id) stay on disk -
 there is no reaper, cleanup is manual. `agent_fabric` resolves the
 messages root lazily per sweep (was: pinned to the launch cwd at
 construction), and pending records migrate across a root change, so a
 session-folder adoption carries the reminders along instead of
 stranding them under the launch cwd.


  The `## Agent messaging` prompt section (prompts messaging_section.md, CLI +
  app variants) tells the model its own mailbox address. Turn-boundary
  delivery: `Agent.externalSteeringSource`
  merges inbox drains into the steering poll (main in AgentCli/AgentService
  as `_mainInboxMessages`, children via the executor) — messages land as
  sender-attributed user messages, so they persist in the session and read
  like a chat. Idle wake: an inbox watcher (2s CLI / 3s app) starts a turn
  when mail arrives while idle — two Fa instances chat live; a 10-run
  streak cap without user input breaks agent-to-agent ping-pong loops.
  The lanes live in `InboxWakePolicy` (gh-1180): user-kind mail always
  wakes and resets the streak (gating it would deadlock:
  no run → no reset → no run); a delivered `schedule_message`
  self-reminder (`[scheduled] ` prefix, from == to) is EXEMPT from the
  cap — a deliberate agent-chosen cadence (night watch, periodic sweep)
  wakes forever, with a 30s cadence floor so a zero-delay re-schedule
  spin is still bounded like chatter; foreign agent chatter stays
  capped. A refused wake is never silent: one dim `[mail] wake refused`
  line per episode and a `wake_refused` receipt.

# Runner split (gh-1005, 2026-09-30): pure-Dart AND all PTY/terminal jobs ->
# ubuntu-24.04-arm (public repo: free, SEPARATE capacity pool from the x64
# queue). Flutter-test legs on arm64 bootstrap the SDK via git clone — Flutter
# ships NO official linux-arm64 SDK (stable manifest is x64 only;
# subosito/flutter-action fails 'version: any architecture: arm64'); x64
# Flutter jobs keep the action. The self-hosted M5 pool is ONE runner
# (fa-m5-1, user LaunchAgent) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work:
# cube-kernel-live. PR PTY legs (integration shards, coverage/duration gates,
# Terminal visual) run hosted-Linux only and never wait on fa-m5-1.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    # gh-1537: NO `branches: [main]` here — the post-merge main CI run is
    # retired. The SM's pre-merge validation dispatch (machine-sm.yml ->
    # factory-sm, strictly serialized) validates the exact tree that
    # merges, so a main-push run would be pure repetition; retiring it
    # kills the duplicate wall time AND the release-bot-commit churn that
    # retriggered it (#1522 lands the tag-sourced versions). The v* tag
    # push stays: the release pipeline (publish/binaries) keys on it, and
    # the full quality gate runs on the tag BEFORE anything publishes.
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (cuts the annotated tag + GitHub Release directly, gh-1522) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the
  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    # gh-1551: the schedule tick IS the release arming mechanism (gh-1537
    # retired the post-merge main run) — but a tick with zero commits on
    # main since the last v* tag has nothing to release, so the
    # `release-pending` pre-check job short-circuits the whole quality
    # gate in seconds (every leg shows SKIPPED explicitly, the run stays
    # green — never a silent absence, never 35-40 min for an empty tick).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Tag/schedule
# runs are never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   installer-portability → gh-1596 REG-1/REG-2: the POSIX-dialect proof
#               for the first-run wizard (site/** or the generator
#               touched) — dash + busybox ash on ubuntu, bash on macOS;
#               red blocks the merge via the quality-gate platform class
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
#   release-pending → gh-1551 empty-tick short-circuit: the schedule is
#                the release arming mechanism (gh-1537), but a tick with
#                no commits since the last v* tag skips the whole gate
#                in seconds (see the job comment below)
# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,
#   integration) are unchanged in semantics — they just need the new aggregate.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal default — every job that needs more
# declares its own job-level permissions block.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # gh-1551: slim the 2h schedule tick. The schedule is the release arming
  # mechanism (gh-1537 retired the post-merge main run), but a tick with
  # ZERO commits on main since the last v* tag has nothing to release —
  # running the full ~35-40 min quality gate for it is pure waste against
  # the shift-left / zero-duplicate-runs principle (observed: run
  # 38147581679, 2026-10-11). This cheap pre-check (~10-30 s: one checkout
  # + git rev-list) compares main HEAD against the latest semver v* tag and
  # exports `pending`; every gate leg ANDs the output into its `if`, so an
  # empty tick short-circuits the whole graph in seconds — legs show
  # SKIPPED explicitly (visible in the run, never silently absent) and the
  # run stays green.
  #
  # Arms that must NEVER be blocked (gh-1551 AC3): v* tag pushes,
  # `release: published` events and both dispatch arms (releaseDryRun /
  # releaseDispatch — incl. every SM validation dispatch, which is a
  # workflow_dispatch on the PR head). All of them short-circuit to
  # pending=true BEFORE the checkout — they do not even pay the fetch, and
  # the gate graph is byte-identical to gh-1537 for them.
  #
  # Fail-open (AC4): `pending` defaults to true and is flipped to false
  # only inside the zero-commits branch — a flaky pre-check (tag fetch
  # hiccup, rev-list error) degrades to the full gate with a loud warning,
  # never to a silently suppressed release. The check itself never
  # reddens the run: only an infra-level failure (the checkout itself)
  # does, which is honest.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  release-pending:
    name: Release pending check (gh-1551)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      pending: ${{ steps.check.outputs.pending }}
    steps:
      # Tag math needs the full tag graph + main HEAD; blobless per
      # gh-1477 (commit metadata only — the exact incantation the static
      # stamp rehearsal uses). Schedule events only: every other arm
      # short-circuits in the script and must not pay the fetch.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: github.event_name == 'schedule'
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none
      - id: check
        env:
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
        run: |
          pending=true
          if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "schedule" ]; then
            # Same semver-tag selection as the static stamp rehearsal
            # below. A schedule checkout IS main's tip (the default
            # branch), so HEAD is exactly "origin/main HEAD" for the
            # comparison the ticket asks for.
            latest=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || true)
            if [ -z "$latest" ]; then
              echo "::warning::no semver v* tag found — treating the tick as release-pending (first-release arm)"
            else
              head_sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
              new_commits=$(git rev-list --count "$latest"..HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo -1)
              echo "latest tag: $latest"
              echo "main HEAD:  $head_sha"
              echo "commits on main since tag: $new_commits"
              if [ "$new_commits" -eq 0 ]; then
                echo "::notice::empty schedule tick — nothing landed on main since $latest; the quality gate and release short-circuit (gh-1551)"
                pending=false
              elif [ "$new_commits" -lt 0 ]; then
                echo "::warning::git rev-list against $latest failed — fail-open, running the full gate"
              fi
            fi
          else
            echo "$EVENT_NAME arm — the pending check never blocks tag pushes, release events or dispatch arms (gh-1551)"
          fi
          echo "release pending: $pending"
          echo "pending=$pending" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  changes:
    name: Classify changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: release-pending
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips the classifier too — every downstream leg is gated on
    # release-pending and would skip anyway, so classifying would be
    # wasted work (and a skipped classifier with empty outputs would
    # wave every changes-keyed leg past its path gate).
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      core: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.core || steps.filter.outputs.core }}
      app: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.app || steps.filter.outputs.app }}
      docs: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.docs || steps.filter.outputs.docs }}
      shared: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.shared || steps.filter.outputs.shared }}
      # PR-only (issue #303): a trajectory-touching diff flips this on so
      # the perf-gate leg below runs the #262 DoD gate per-merge.
      perf: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.perf }}
      # PR-only (gh-1241 REG-1): a trajectory/session/usage-touching diff
      # runs the usage-fold suite per-merge.
      usagefold: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.usagefold }}
      # Issue #1267 N1: the macOS exclusion-zone path set — live on
      # pull_request events AND on SM validation dispatches: the paths
      # step derives the validated diff from merge-base(origin/main, HEAD)
      # when no pull_request context exists (fail-safe — a classification
      # failure runs the leg, never skips it).
      exzone: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.exzone }}
      # Issue #1267 N2: the diff modified flutter_app/pubspec.lock — the
      # transitive-drift vector that kept linux/windows release builds red
      # for five nights (#1265). Same path-triggered model as exzone.
      locksmoke: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.locksmoke }}
      # PR-only (issue #551): test/integration/** changes run the no-key
      # mock-LLM integration legs per-PR instead of at tag time only.
      intmock: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.intmock }}
      # gh-1596 REG-1/REG-2: a diff touching the installer generation
      # pipeline (site/** or scripts/gen_installers.dart) runs the
      # sh-portability legs — template lint, golden drift, and the piped
      # wizard under dash (ubuntu) / bash (macOS).
      installer: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.installer }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # base...head diff for the classifier below
          # gh-1477: blobless — historical blobs are never read; git
          # lazy-fetches the rare blob a diff actually touches.
          filter: blob:none
      # Non-PR events (tags, schedule, dispatch): everything is
      # affected — the full gate always guards releases. Since gh-1537
      # there are NO main-push events at all; the SM validation dispatch
      # (workflow_dispatch on the rebased PR head) is the pre-merge gate
      # and lands in this arm, so every validation runs the whole-tree
      # gates (crap4dart baseline, coverage ratchet, jscpd) — nothing was
      # ever main-only.
      - id: filter
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        run: |
          echo "core=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "app=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "docs=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "shared=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      # PR classification runs through THE SAME classifier the pre-commit
      # hook uses (issue #194, AC7 + AC5/E2): one source of truth for path
      # rules, and the unknown-path safe default (full gate) — e.g. a new
      # dart_test.yaml at the repo root — now holds in CI, not only in the
      # hook. The selected stage set maps back to the same four groups the
      # old dorny filter emitted.
      - id: paths
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
        env:
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          # ── Issue #1267 N1/N2 dispatch arm ──────────────────────────────
          # SM validation dispatches carry NO pull_request event context,
          # so BASE_REF/HEAD_REF are empty there: derive the validated diff
          # from git — merge-base(origin/main, HEAD) is the PR fork point
          # (the checkout above is fetch-depth: 0, so origin/main exists).
          # merge-base == HEAD (a main dispatch, or an already-merged
          # branch) diffs to nothing and the narrowed arms skip. A failed
          # resolve fails SAFE: both arms run unconditioned —
          # over-triggering a rare-path leg costs minutes, under-triggering
          # one hides a nightly-only red (the #1309 class).
          if [ -z "$HEAD_REF" ]; then
            HEAD_REF="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
            BASE_REF="$(git merge-base origin/main "$HEAD_REF" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            if [ -z "$BASE_REF" ]; then
              echo "::warning::merge-base(origin/main, HEAD) failed on the dispatch checkout — failing safe: exzone + locksmoke arms run"
              echo "exzone=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo "locksmoke=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo "installer=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              exit 0
            fi
          fi
          # Issue #1267 N1: the macOS exclusion-zone path set. Gated on
          # BOTH pull_request events and SM validation dispatches (the
          # legs below consult these outputs on either event). Context:
          # the ubuntu flutter-tests leg runs this family but every
          # engine-dependent test SKIPS there (native_test_guard.dart finds
          # no QuickJS .so on a bare runner); they truly execute only on
          # macOS — the hole #1309 escaped through (gh-1307). The issue's
          # packages/js_widget_runtime/** is an EXTERNAL repo now, so its
          # bumps arrive via the flutter_app/pubspec.yaml pin.
          if git diff --name-only "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_REF" |
              grep -qE '(^flutter_app/lib/apps/|^lib/src/js_ext/|^flutter_app/test/apps/|^flutter_app/test/native_test_guard\.dart$|^flutter_app/pubspec\.yaml$)'; then
            echo "exzone=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          # Issue #1267 N2 (AC2): the lockfile-refresh vector — resolution
          # floats transitive deps to latest-compatible, and the breaking
          # arrival (#1265: a transitive flutter_inappwebview) lands as a
          # flutter_app/pubspec.lock diff with nothing else changed. The
          # flutter-app-lock-smoke legs are the pre-merge net; PRs not
          # touching the lockfile never pay for them.
          if git diff --name-only "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_REF" |
              grep -qE '^flutter_app/pubspec\.lock$'; then
            echo "locksmoke=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          # gh-1596 REG-1/REG-2: the installer generation pipeline — every
          # sh artifact under site/ and the generator that renders them.
          # Gated on the SAME two events as exzone/locksmoke (pull_request
          # + validation dispatch); the classifier failure arm above runs
          # it fail-safe.
          if git diff --name-only "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_REF" |
              grep -qE '(^site/|^scripts/gen_installers\.dart$)'; then
            echo "installer=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" != "pull_request" ]; then
            # Dispatch done — the stages classifier below reads a
            # pull_request event's base/head only; on dispatches the group
            # outputs stay with the non-PR filter step (full gate).
            exit 0
          fi
          stages=$(scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run |
            sed -n 's/^Fast gate scope: .*stages://p')
          echo "gate stages:[$stages]"
          # Empty output can only mean detection failure: full gate.
          [ -z "$(echo $stages)" ] && stages="size analyze test-core coverage crap dup dupx flutter integration-mock"
          case " $stages " in *"flutter"*) echo "app=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          case " $stages " in *"test-core"*) echo "core=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          case " $stages " in *"analyze"*) echo "docs=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          # Issue #551: test/integration changes select the mock-LLM leg.
          case " $stages " in *"integration-mock"*) echo "intmock=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          # All nine stages selected = a shared/unknown path changed:
          if [ -z "$(echo $stages)" ]; then
            # Empty output can only mean detection failure: full gate.
            stages="size analyze test-core coverage crap dup dupx flutter integration-mock"
          fi
          if [ "$(echo $stages | wc -w)" -eq 9 ]; then
            echo "shared=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          # Issue #303: the #262 DoD perf gate must red-block the MERGE for
          # trajectory regressions, not only the release — before #551 the
          # only integration leg outside PRs was tag-time. The perf-gate
          # leg re-selects the same gate via --tags perf. Paths = everything
          # the #262 fix touched: ledger core, fa_ui trajectory widgets, CLI
          # trajectory parts, the fah entrypoint, its tests, and the app's
          # session load path.
          if git diff --name-only "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_REF" |
              grep -qE '(^lib/src/trajectory/|^packages/fa_ui/lib/src/trajectory/|^lib/src/cli/trajectory_|^bin/fah\.dart$|^test/(integration/)?trajectory/|^flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service(_sessions)?\.dart$)'; then
            echo "perf=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          # gh-1241 REG-1: the usage fold consumes the trajectory ledger's
          # model_request_summary records and the session chain's shape —
          # a red usage-fold suite blocks the merge even when the regular
          # legs are green.
          if git diff --name-only "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_REF" |
              grep -qE '(^lib/src/trajectory/|^lib/src/session/|^lib/src/usage/|^test/usage/|^lib/src/cli/agent_cli_usage_ledger\.dart$)'; then
            echo "usagefold=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Issue #709: live kernel-mode cube legs. The ubuntu test-core shards can
  # only prove the SBPL PROFILE TEXT (unit + guard/profile parity) — the
  # kernel's last-match-wins read/write enforcement of rw mounts under a
  # read-denied prefix needs a real `sandbox-exec` run, which exists only on
  # macOS. Both live suites skip with a NAMED reason wherever they cannot
  # run (no sandbox-exec / already-sandboxed host / HOME outside /Users) —
  # the skip lands in the job log, never silent; this leg is where they
  # actually execute. The leg is a real gate input: `quality-gate` NEEDS it
  # and fails the merge when it fails (a skip — a diff with no core paths —
  # passes, like every other optional leg).
  #
  # Skip condition note (PR #718 review): gating on `core` covers
  # `shared`-only diffs too — the classifier maps a shared/unknown path to
  # ALL nine stages, `test-core` among them, so `core=true` falls out and
  # this leg runs; only docs-only diffs (or non-PR context mismatches)
  # skip it.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  cube-kernel-live:
    name: Cube kernel live (macOS)
    runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - run: dart pub get

      # Content-addressed native-assets hook downloads (sqlite3 et al) are
      # hash-verified on reuse — cache them so a GitHub release-asset
      # brownout (504 bodies hashed as mismatches, 2026-09-21) can't
      # re-break every job that re-downloads.
      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: dart test cube backends (live kernel legs)
        run: dart test test/cube/backends

      # gh-1059 AC4: the real-keychain runner guard — `security`
      # add/find/delete against the runner's login keychain through the
      # bounded-helper machinery (outcome classification incl. stderr
      # tails, env merge, timeout kill). The group is tagged `integration`
      # (real side effects), so the Linux core shards and the pre-commit
      # gate skip it; this macOS leg is where it actually executes. Skips
      # with a named reason when no `security` binary / default keychain.
      - name: dart test secure key store (macOS Keychain live legs)
        run: dart test test/secrets/secure_key_store_test.dart --tags integration

  static:
    name: Static gates
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 8
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1538: the publish dry-run below rehearses the tag-stamped
          # stage (gh-1522), moved here from the retired nightly
          # full-quality leg — tag math needs the full tag graph
          # (blobless per gh-1477, same incantation that leg used).
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get

      # Issue #1234: the ≤2800-line file guard MOVED into crap4dart's loc
      # gate (crap4dart.yaml, wc -l parity verified by the maintainer
      # recipe in the issue) — enforced whole-tree by the
      # `crap4dart check --baseline` Quality-gates step below. The shell
      # find-exec guard (gh-1232 AC2) is gone: one enforcement point, no
      # drifted exclusions.

      # Issue #1100: the fa-web-spa.zip packaging guard (base-tag patch +
      # absolute-/app/ grep) must stay functional on every PR — a release
      # run is the wrong place to first discover a broken guard. Fixture
      # self-test: positive path + all red exits, pure bash, no web build.
      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"
          for f in flutter_service_worker.js flutter_bootstrap.js; do echo "// $f" > "$d/build/$f"; done
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null
          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'
          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's
          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"
          # Red exit 1: an absolute /app/ sneaking into a touchpoint.
          echo '{"x":"/app/y"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed a build containing /app/ (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 2: no base tag to patch.
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          echo '<html></html>' > "$d/build/index.html"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad2.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an unpatchable base tag (AC1 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 3: a missing touchpoint file.
          rm "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad3.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an incomplete build (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # fa1.dev parity pin: both web builds must keep the identical
          # release flags AND the same pinned SDK — the bundle's only edit
          # stays the base tag. (#1431): the SDK pin must be an EXACT
          # 3.47.x patch (no wildcard) — a floating patch re-resolves a new
          # engine build and moves the canvaskit/skwasm rev-hash dir the
          # size gates track.
          for wf in .github/workflows/pages.yml .github/workflows/ci.yml; do
            grep -q -- '--release' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost the --release web flag (#1100 parity)"; exit 1; }
            grep -q -- '--base-href /app/' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost --base-href /app/ (#1100 parity, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }
            grep -Eq "flutter-version: '3\.47\.[0-9]+'" "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf unpinned Flutter SDK (#1100 parity + #1431 exact-patch rule, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }
          done

      # Issue #433 AC1: README CRAP badge must equal the crap4dart.yaml
      # threshold (they drifted to 8.0-vs-12.0 once). Pure python — runs on
      # every PR, including docs-only ones (a README edit is exactly the
      # drift vector).
      - name: CRAP badge/config sync guard
        run: python3 scripts/check_crap_guards.py

      # gh-1476 AC5 (PR #1479 owner directive): the GEO layer is built at
      # deploy time — gitignored, never committed, nothing to drift
      # against. So the gate builds to a temp dir and validates the
      # OUTPUT: test/site/* (no-JS crawl, robots contract, sitemap
      # integrity, JSON-LD, llms guards) serve the temp tree over loopback
      # HTTP via FA_SITE_ROOT. Stronger than the old `--check` drift gate:
      # it tests the builder itself, and hand-edited generated HTML is
      # uncommittable by construction.
      - name: GEO site build + validation (gh-1476 AC5)
        run: |
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          # The builder's post input is the site/blog/posts COPY of the
          # canonical blog/posts — keep them pinned together so the gate
          # can never validate a stale or hand-edited copy (gh-1476
          # review). PRE-sync diff: an in-place edit of the copy is red
          # (the deploy's build_blog would silently discard it). Sync,
          # then POST-sync diff: a new or edited canonical post that was
          # never copied into site/blog/posts is red.
          git diff --exit-code -- site/blog/posts site/blog/posts.json
          dart scripts/build_blog.dart
          git diff --exit-code -- site/blog/posts site/blog/posts.json
          dart scripts/build_site.dart --out "$d/site"
          FA_SITE_ROOT="$d/site" dart test test/site/

      # gh-1199 AC2: the deterministic-gate boundary is self-enforcing —
      # an integration-tagged test that looks live (real provider URL, or
      # a credential-key literal with no mock/loopback in sight) without
      # the `llm` tag fails the gate. Runs on every PR: a PR adding a live
      # test (E1) is exactly the diff this must catch.
      - name: LLM tag boundary lint (gh-1199 AC2)
        run: python3 scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py

      # gh-1199 AC6/E3: the flake quarantine list itself must stay
      # honest — every entry documented (issue, since, >=2 proving runs)
      # and pointing at an existing integration-tagged file.
      - name: Flake quarantine list guard (gh-1199 AC6)
        run: python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py --check

      # gh-1296 NG1/AC2: every lockfile in the repo is committed and
      # enforced — ONE inventory list (scripts/check_lockfiles.sh) fails the
      # PR when a listed lockfile is missing, untracked, or gitignored, and
      # the guard's own red exits are fixture-self-tested so the check
      # cannot rot silently (#1100 pattern).
      - name: Lockfile inventory gate (gh-1296 NG1)
        run: bash scripts/check_lockfiles.sh inventory

      # gh-1522 AC5: committed pubspecs carry the FIXED 0.0.0-dev
      # placeholder — the git tag is the single source of truth and CI
      # stamps the staged publish tree from it. A hand-bumped version in
      # either pubspec is a mistake now: it desyncs the tag↔staged-file
      # invariant the publish stamper relies on (and reintroduces the
      # lockfile churn gh-1522 retires). Runs on every PR — a bump attempt
      # is exactly the diff this must catch.
      - name: Version placeholder guard (gh-1522)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          for f in pubspec.yaml flutter_app/pubspec.yaml; do
            v=$(grep '^version:' "$f" | awk '{print $2}')
            base="${v%%+*}"
            if [ "$base" != "0.0.0-dev" ]; then
              echo "::error::$f carries '$v' — the committed version must stay the 0.0.0-dev placeholder (gh-1522). Releases are tags; CI stamps the real version at publish/build time."
              exit 1
            fi
          done

      - name: Lockfile gate self-test (gh-1296 AC2)
        run: bash scripts/check_lockfiles_selftest.sh

      # gh-1300 AC6: the shard duration-budget gate's own red exits are
      # fixture-self-tested (breach fails + files the body; fit passes;
      # warn band; unbudgeted shard is loud; update is down-only) so the
      # ratchet cannot rot silently (#1100 pattern).
      - name: Duration budget gate self-test (gh-1300 AC6)
        run: bash scripts/duration_budget_selftest.sh

      # gh-1364: the flake watcher's issue dedup is fixture-self-tested
      # against a stubbed gh (no network) — a tracker whose title carries
      # the `(#<digits>...` suffix GitHub search silently cannot see is
      # still found (no --search anywhere; dedup keys on the body's
      # **File**: path, not the truncated title), a create landing beside
      # an existing open tracker closes itself and fails loudly, a closed
      # tracker is re-opened instead of re-filed next to, and runs already
      # in comments are not re-commented (#1100 pattern).
      - name: Flake watcher dedup self-test (gh-1364)
        run: bash scripts/flake_watch_selftest.sh

      # gh-1568: the SM merge guard's gh-side lookups are fixture-tested
      # against the REAL commits-API shape (tree nested under `commit`)
      # on a PATH-stubbed gh — the `.tree.sha` jq bug false-alarmed every
      # merge-commit landing, and the missing conclusion field made the
      # live path alarm on every push. Covers tree/head/race/404 paths
      # and the self-diagnosing alarm body (#1100 pattern).
      - name: SM merge guard self-test (gh-1568)
        run: bash scripts/sm_merge_guard_selftest.sh

      # #1431: the size-budget gate's own red exits are fixture-tested
      # (#1100 pattern) — an engine rev-hash rename must UPDATE not NEW,
      # vendored engine churn warns instead of reddening, first-party
      # payload still fails hard, and the 20+hex regex leaves first-party
      # paths that merely contain hex alone.
      - name: Size manifest gate self-test (#1431)
        run: python3 scripts/test_size_manifest.py

      # Full analyze needs the example app's package config (Flutter imports);
      # a docs-only PR skips the flutter setup entirely and analyzes the pure
      # Dart scopes only — it cannot have changed resolution anyway.
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Example app setup (full analyze only)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          printf 'OPENROUTER_API_KEY=\nMODEL_ID=\nBASE_URL=\nHUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=\n' > [REDACTED:Credential File]
          cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
          dart pub get --directory=office_addin/dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
      - name: dart analyze (full)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        # pana score: infos dock points — keep zero
        run: dart analyze --fatal-infos --fatal-warnings

      - name: dart analyze (docs-only scope)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        # pana score: infos dock points — keep zero
        run: dart analyze --fatal-infos --fatal-warnings lib test bin

      # Publish gate at PR time: publish-blocking problems (undeclared lib/
      # imports, stray PEM-like strings) used to surface only in the tag-time
      # publish job — the v0.1.331 era: an undeclared package:cryptography
      # import shipped red on ~26 consecutive tags. --ignore-warnings: the
      # two known layout warnings (gitignored install_local.sh, docs/
      # naming) must not redden every PR, while validation ERRORS — "does
      # not have X in the dependencies section of pubspec.yaml" — still
      # fail. setup-dart (sdk >= 3.13) registers a publish-scoped PUB_TOKEN
      # job-wide and pub.dev rejects authenticated metadata reads, so
      # resolve unauthenticated (same pattern as the publish job);
      # --dry-run never uploads.
      - name: Publish dry-run (unauthenticated)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          dart pub token remove https://pub.dev || true
          # Against the STAGED tree, not the repo root (#597 AC1): the
          # publish job publishes from the stage — the v0.1.407 class of
          # failure (staged resolution re-pinning vendor/dart_tui through
          # pubspec_overrides.yaml) must redden the PR, not the tag.
          bash scripts/stage_publish_package.sh /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage
          # gh-1538: the STAMP rehearsal moved here from the retired nightly
          # full-quality leg — the pre-merge gate is the single test gate
          # now, so a stamp failure (placeholder leak, changelog-section
          # generation, staged-version desync, cap trim) must redden the
          # PR, not surface at tag time. Rehearses the NEXT tag's payload
          # exactly like the nightly leg did (gh-1522).
          latest=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1)
          latest="${latest#v}"
          IFS='.' read -r major minor patch <<< "$latest"
          next="$major.$minor.$((patch + 1))"
          echo "rehearsing the stamp of the NEXT tag: v$next"
          bash scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage "$next"
          # The staged tree must ANALYZE clean: v0.1.411 shipped files
          # with broken imports (the staging filter pruned lib/src/memory;
          # imports of fork-only dart_tui symbols) that only a consumer's
          # `dart analyze` ever surfaced (issue #613). Errors fail the
          # gate; warnings/infos pass, matching the static analyze stage.
          (cd /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage && dart pub get && dart analyze)
          (cd /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage && dart pub publish --dry-run --ignore-warnings)

  test-core:
    # Always runs (no job-level path gate): a path-filtered matrix skip
    # posts a check-run with the LITERAL unrendered name — the required
    # contexts (shard 0..3) never report, and branch protection blocks
    # out-of-scope PRs at 27 green checks. The scope fastpass below
    # green-skips the real steps in seconds instead.
    name: Core tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    timeout-minutes: 12
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: echo "no core/shared changes — shard green-skipped (required context reported)"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Pub cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage
          test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart
          test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          name: coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2

      # junit durations for the weekly shard-rebalance.yml (retention 7d so
      # a quiet week never starves it into the file-count fallback).
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          name: junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
          retention-days: 7

  # Issue #551: the no-key integration legs (MockLlmServer scenarios, PTY
  # harness, no secrets, no network) run per-PR whenever test/integration/**
  # changes — the #538 rot class (legs breaking silently between releases,
  # discovered only at tag time) becomes a red PR at the commit that broke
  # them. Real-provider legs carry the `llm` tag and stay in the tag-only
  # provider-smoke job; perf has its own #303 trajectory gate; browser-ext
  # its own workflow. `pty` marks child-agent-spawn tests whose second
  # process boot is unbounded under runner load (issue #553, red twice on
  # this leg) — they stay in nightly's pty-integration job.
  integration-mock:
    name: Integration tests (mock LLM)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    timeout-minutes: 25
    permissions:
      contents: read
    if: needs.changes.outputs.intmock == 'true' && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

# gh-1625: [INFRA] ci.yml double-fires the full quality gate on release tags (push v* + release published) — dedupe the release-event run to binaries-only

## Description

## Symptom

Tag `v1.0.580` produced **two CI runs** (2026-10-15 05:29Z):

- run 38687023638 — `CI`, event **push**, ref v1.0.580 — in_progress (the full quality gate, by design: gate the tag before anything publishes)
- run 38687023803 — `CI`, event **release**, ref v1.0.580 — pending (the SAME full quality gate again)

Policy (owner): CI runs **once**, pre-merge (via the SM); no double runs on tags, main, or releases. Main-push CI is already retired (gh-1537) and PR CI is dispatch-only — but the **tag double-fire is still there**, and it doubles the release wall time on the exact artifact we ship.

## Why it happens

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` has two triggers that legitimately fire on one release:

1. `push: tags: ['v*']` — the release pipeline keys on the tag; the full quality gate runs on the tag BEFORE anything publishes (gh-1537/gh-1172 design).
2. `release: types: [published]` — added to build + attach the binaries matrix when a release is created (web UI / API / auto-release).

The file's own comment acknowledges the collision: "Pushed tags also arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins)." — i.e. only the **binaries upload** was made idempotent, but the **entire quality matrix re-runs** on the release event. The schedule tick has a `release-pending` pre-check short-circuit; the release event has nothing.

## Fix direction

Dedupe the release-event run, keep its reason to exist:

- **Pre-check job** (`release-dedupe`, mirrors the `release-pending` pattern): runs only on `github.event_name == 'release'`. It checks whether a CI run for the same tag ref (or head SHA) already exists from the `push` event (`gh run list --branch <tag> --event push`, within a recent window).
  - exists (any status) → output `dedupe=true`; the release run **skips every quality leg** (static/test/coverage/guards/flutter) and executes **only the binaries-attach leg** (idempotent `--clobber`, last-wins as today). Fast, seconds-to-minutes.
  - not exists (release cut on an OLD tag, no fresh push) → `dedupe=false`; the release run executes the full gate as today — that path stays the safety net.
- Quality legs get `needs: [release-dedupe]` + `if: needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'` (no-op on push/dispatch/schedule events).
- Keep the documented "tag runs are never cancelled mid-flight" concurrency rule untouched.

## Acceptance

- **AC1** — annotated tag push → release published: exactly ONE full-gate run (the push run); the release run short-circuits to binaries-attach. Two workflow runs may still appear, but the second runs no quality legs.
- **AC2** — release published on an existing old tag (no fresh push): full gate still runs (dedupe=false path).
- **AC3** — push/dispatch/schedule behavior unchanged (PR SM validation, nightly, dry-run arms).
- **AC4** — no race window where BOTH runs attach different binaries: the `--clobber` last-wins semantics preserved and covered by a dry-run log assertion or workflow-lint check.
- **AC5** — the dedupe pre-check fails safe: on `gh run list` API error it outputs `dedupe=false` (full gate runs) rather than skipping blindly.

## Regression guard

A workflow-lint/CI-selftest assertion (aab-gate-selftest pattern) asserting the release-event path short-circuits when a push-run exists for the tag.

Refs: #1522, #1551 (schedule arming), gh-1537 (main-run retirement), gh-1172 (release dispatch).

Assignee: ai-teammate.

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone

# Runner split (gh-1005, 2026-09-30): pure-Dart AND all PTY/terminal jobs ->
# ubuntu-24.04-arm (public repo: free, SEPARATE capacity pool from the x64
# queue). Flutter-test legs on arm64 bootstrap the SDK via git clone — Flutter
# ships NO official linux-arm64 SDK (stable manifest is x64 only;
# subosito/flutter-action fails 'version: any architecture: arm64'); x64
# Flutter jobs keep the action. The self-hosted M5 pool is ONE runner
# (fa-m5-1, user LaunchAgent) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work:
# cube-kernel-live. PR PTY legs (integration shards, coverage/duration gates,
# Terminal visual) run hosted-Linux only and never wait on fa-m5-1.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    # gh-1537: NO `branches: [main]` here — the post-merge main CI run is
    # retired. The SM's pre-merge validation dispatch (machine-sm.yml ->
    # factory-sm, strictly serialized) validates the exact tree that
    # merges, so a main-push run would be pure repetition; retiring it
    # kills the duplicate wall time AND the release-bot-commit churn that
    # retriggered it (#1522 lands the tag-sourced versions). The v* tag
    # push stays: the release pipeline (publish/binaries) keys on it, and
    # the full quality gate runs on the tag BEFORE anything publishes.
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (cuts the annotated tag + GitHub Release directly, gh-1522) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the
  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    # gh-1551: the schedule tick IS the release arming mechanism (gh-1537
    # retired the post-merge main run) — but a tick with zero commits on
    # main since the last v* tag has nothing to release, so the
    # `release-pending` pre-check job short-circuits the whole quality
    # gate in seconds (every leg shows SKIPPED explicitly, the run stays
    # green — never a silent absence, never 35-40 min for an empty tick).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Tag/schedule
# runs are never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   installer-portability → gh-1596 REG-1/REG-2: the POSIX-dialect proof
#               for the first-run wizard (site/** or the generator
#               touched) — dash + busybox ash on ubuntu, bash on macOS;
#               red blocks the merge via the quality-gate platform class
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
#   release-pending → gh-1551 empty-tick short-circuit: the schedule is
#                the release arming mechanism (gh-1537), but a tick with
#                no commits since the last v* tag skips the whole gate
#                in seconds (see the job comment below)
# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,
#   integration) are unchanged in semantics — they just need the new aggregate.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal default — every job that needs more
# declares its own job-level permissions block.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # gh-1551: slim the 2h schedule tick. The schedule is the release arming
  # mechanism (gh-1537 retired the post-merge main run), but a tick with
  # ZERO commits on main since the last v* tag has nothing to release —
  # running the full ~35-40 min quality gate for it is pure waste against
  # the shift-left / zero-duplicate-runs principle (observed: run
  # 38147581679, 2026-10-11). This cheap pre-check (~10-30 s: one checkout
  # + git rev-list) compares main HEAD against the latest semver v* tag and
  # exports `pending`; every gate leg ANDs the output into its `if`, so an
  # empty tick short-circuits the whole graph in seconds — legs show
  # SKIPPED explicitly (visible in the run, never silently absent) and the
  # run stays green.
  #
  # Arms that must NEVER be blocked (gh-1551 AC3): v* tag pushes,
  # `release: published` events and both dispatch arms (releaseDryRun /
  # releaseDispatch — incl. every SM validation dispatch, which is a
  # workflow_dispatch on the PR head). All of them short-circuit to
  # pending=true BEFORE the checkout — they do not even pay the fetch, and
  # the gate graph is byte-identical to gh-1537 for them.
  #
  # Fail-open (AC4): `pending` defaults to true and is flipped to false
  # only inside the zero-commits branch — a flaky pre-check (tag fetch
  # hiccup, rev-list error) …

# dmtools ai-teammate runner exports FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG /
  # FAH_PROVIDER, which used to decide test fate through the args resolver.
  # Run the non-integration suite under the same hostile env so any
  # ambient-env read that leaks back into resolution regresses loudly.
  # gh-1198 rework: the runner now ALSO exports FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE (the
  # provider-queue env won over the file queue and silently flipped the
  # /providers queue editor tests to the env-wins refusal on the PR head) —
  # the var rides the same hostile block so a future ambient read of it
  # regresses here, not only on the runner.
  hostile-env:
    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai
      FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: '{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnvVar":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}'
      FAH_PROVIDER: zai
      FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE: '[{"provider_type":"zai","provider_config":{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnv":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}}]'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: dart test under hostile ambient env
        run: dart test --exclude-tags integration

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Nightly parity (2026-09-23): the two legs that stayed nightly-only went
  # red on main night after night before anyone looked — the CLI-coverage
  # ratchet (12.07% < 12.17%) and the Terminal-visual PTY suite (five
  # regressions, several cascading out of fixed-port collisions). Both legs
  # are part of the COMMON PR suite: they run on every CI invocation (the
  # Machine SM dispatches ci.yml per PR head), unconditioned by path — a
  # diff that breaks them must red-block THE PR, never the 3:30 nightly.
  # gh-1538: nightly is builds + integration-only now — this PR leg IS the
  # only Terminal-visual run (the nightly cli-visual duplicate is retired).
  # gh-1537 retired the post-merge main CI run, so this pre-merge leg is
  # the only Terminal-visual gate any tree ever sees; nightly's remaining
  # legs are a scheduled backstop, not a second merge gate.
  # gh-1300 (2026-10-06): the PTY/CLI shards pay toolchain+boot ONCE per
  # run, not per test. Every integration test spawns a fresh CLI; JIT
  # `dart bin/fah.dart` cost VM start + CFE kernel compile ~30 s PER SPAWN
  # on loaded ARM runners (the dominant term: 29 files, 3 shards x
  # ~350 s). This job compiles the AOT bundle once, the shards download
  # it and point the FA_BIN seam (test/integration/pty_harness.dart,
  # faCliCommand) at it — spawn ~1 s, per-test isolation untouched (each
  # spawn is still a fresh process with its own env/cwd). The binary MUST
  # match the PR's sources: built fresh in this run, never cached across
  # runs; the shards fail loudly if it is missing or dead (`test -x` +
  # `--version` smoke), never silently fall back to JIT.
  fa-aot-build:
    name: AOT fa binary (compiled once per run, gh-1300)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: release-pending
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      # Same hooks cache key as the shards: the build pays the native
      # assets hooks here so the shard-side restore is warm.
      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: dart build cli (AOT bundle, same shape install_local.sh ships)
        run: |
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=fa-local
          # The installer writes version.txt into the bundle; mirror it so
          # `fa --version` from the AOT binary reports the real version

          # gh-1522: the committed pubspec is the 0.0.0-dev placeholder —
          # PR runs stamp from git describe (falls back to the short sha
          # on shallow checkouts); release runs get the exact tag from the
          # release binaries job.
          version=$(git describe --tags --always --dirty 2>/dev/null || echo 0.0.0-dev)
          version="${version#v}"
          echo "$version" > fa-local/bundle/version.txt
          ./fa-local/bundle/bin/fah --version

          name: fa-aot-bin
          path: fa-local/bundle/
