          EOF

      # Issue #487: cross-module duplication gate (issue body measured 20
      # files shipped as app↔core/fa_ui/browser_ext clones). Runs the SAME
      # stage the pre-commit hook runs — one marker, parity diffable. The
      # app leg matters: most cross-module clones are born on the app side
      # and the CRAP/dup steps above stay core/shared-scoped.
      - name: Cross-module duplication ratchet (issue #487)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true'
        run: scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --stages dupx

      # Issue #135 AC1 evidence: a realistic ~300 MB / 100k-record
      # session (3 branches, image blocks, compaction checkpoints)
      # opens through the windowed storage in bounded time and memory.
      # The timing numbers land in the job log; the bounds assertions
      # make regressions (an accidental full read at open) fail here.
      - name: Windowed-open scale evidence (issue #135 AC1)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          dart run scripts/gen_session_fixture.dart \
            --records 100000 --out /tmp/big-session.jsonl \
            --branches 3 --images --compactions --measure | tee /tmp/ac1.log
          python3 - <<'EOF'
          import re, sys
          log = open('/tmp/ac1.log').read()
          total = int(re.search(r'countRecords: (\d+)', log).group(1))
          resident = int(re.search(r'open\+tail: (\d+)', log).group(1))
          assert total >= 100000, f'unexpected record count {total}'
          # The resident window after open is the tail chunk (200) —
          # a full read at open would report ~100k here.
          assert resident <= 1000, f'open read too much: {resident}'
          print(f'AC1 bounds OK: {total} records, {resident} resident at open')
          EOF

      # Issue #199 evidence: a FULL open of the same fixture through the
      # isolate parse executor matches the inline default (parity asserted
      # in-process), and listing 500 small sessions through the repo's
      # bounded-parallel list stays fast. Bounds are generous CI guards;
      # the real numbers land in the job log for trend tracking.
      - name: Isolate parse + parallel listing evidence (issue #199)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          dart run scripts/gen_session_fixture.dart \
            --records 100000 --out /tmp/big-session.jsonl \
            --branches 3 --images --compactions --measure | tee /tmp/ac199.log
          dart run scripts/gen_session_fixture.dart \
            --list-sessions 500 --out /tmp/sessions-199 | tee /tmp/ac199-list.log
          python3 - <<'EOF'
          import re, sys
          log = open('/tmp/ac199.log').read()
          isolate = int(re.search(r'full-open isolate: (\d+)', log).group(1))
          assert isolate < 120000, f'isolate full-open too slow: {isolate} ms'
          assert 'isolate parity: OK' in log, 'isolate/inline parity mismatch'
          llog = open('/tmp/ac199-list.log').read()
          listed = int(re.search(r'list 500 sessions: (\d+)', llog).group(1))
          assert listed < 5000, f'list of 500 sessions too slow: {listed} ms'
          print(f'AC199 OK: isolate full-open {isolate} ms, '
                f'list 500 sessions {listed} ms')
          EOF

  # Flutter app analyze split out of the test job (was serial pub get →
  # analyze → test in one 6-min job): analyze runs in parallel with the
  # sharded test legs, each leg no longer waits for it.
  flutter-analyze:
    name: Flutter app analyze (ubuntu)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 8
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-

      # .env is gitignored but declared as a Flutter asset (flutter_dotenv);
      # newer flutter validates assets at pub-get/test-build time, so the
      # placeholders must exist BEFORE flutter pub get. Content mirrors the
      # proven build-macos.yml incantation (bare `touch` produced "No file or
      # variants found for asset: .env" on ubuntu/flutter 3.47.4).
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      # firebase_options.dart is gitignored; the tracked placeholder makes it
      # compile (Firebase init is skipped for YOUR_* values at runtime).
      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # gh-1296 NG1: the Podfile.lock half of the lockfile gate. pub get just
      # generated .flutter-plugins-dependencies; the gate fails the PR when a
      # native iOS/macOS plugin resolved by the committed pubspec.lock has no
      # pod in the platform's Podfile.lock, or its pod is pinned at a stale
      # version vs the resolved podspec (the gh-1274 class, plus the
      # flutter_gemma 1.8.0-vs-1.11.3 skew this PR fixed). Self-tested in
      # Static gates (AC2).
      - name: Lockfile pod-sync gate (gh-1296 NG1)
        run: bash scripts/check_lockfiles.sh pod-sync

      # Issue #1234: the flutter_app ≤2800-line guard moved into the app
      # crap4dart.yaml loc gate — enforced whole-tree by the app-crap-gate
      # job's `crap4dart check --baseline` (app_localizations.dart is
      # gen-l10n output, excluded in the gate config). The shell find-exec
      # guard (gh-1232 AC2) is gone.

      - name: flutter analyze
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings

  # flutter_app tests sharded ×2 by a deterministic modulo split of the
  # sorted suite (same file list as before — golden + cli_visual stay out,
  # host-locked): each leg is ~half the test phase; pub-cache shared with
  # flutter-analyze so a warm leg pair reuses downloads.
  flutter-tests:
    name: Flutter app tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    # End-of-run drain can stall minutes under shared-runner load while
    # every test already passed (0 failures, killed mid-drain on #330):
    # fa_ui shards get 12m and flutter_app is the heaviest package.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # arm64: no official linux-arm64 release tarball (x64-only manifest) —
      # subosito/flutter-action cannot fetch stable here. Bootstrap via git
      # clone instead: flutter_tools pulls the official arm64 Dart SDK itself.
      - name: Flutter SDK (arm64 git bootstrap)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          git clone --depth 1 -b stable https://github.com/flutter/flutter.git "$HOME/flutter"
          echo "$HOME/flutter/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          export PATH="$HOME/flutter/bin:$PATH"
          flutter --version
          flutter precache
      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-

      # See flutter-analyze: placeholder must exist before pub get.
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # Golden suite is intentionally NOT here: goldens are host-locked
      # (same macOS host renders them differently across minor SDKs — see the
      # dynamic_messages saga) and would all redden on ubuntu. Widget/unit
      # tests run here on a cheap runner; goldens stay guarded by
      # build-macos.yml and the nightly full matrix (issue #177 E5/OQ3:
      # pinned-font golden migration is a follow-up, not this card).
      - name: flutter test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
        # Goldens stay out (host-locked, see the golden comment above).
        # Native-dependent tests (quickjs_c_bridge .so, mic channel) are NOT
        # excluded — issue #184 made them host-portable via the skip guard in
        # flutter_app/test/native_test_guard.dart + the injected-ASR fix.
        # Deterministic modulo split of the sorted file list: shard i takes
        # lines where NR % 2 == i — union == the old single job's list.
        run: |
          cd flutter_app
          find test -name '*_test.dart' ! -path '*/golden/*' ! -path '*/cli_visual/*' \
            | sort | awk -v i=${{ matrix.shard }} 'NR % 2 == i' > shard-files.txt
          echo "shard files: $(wc -l < shard-files.txt)"
          # --coverage (issue #433): each shard emits lcov for the
          # app-crap-gate job; the covered surface matches the CRAP
          # sources [lib] exactly.
          flutter test --exclude-tags integration --coverage $(cat shard-files.txt)

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: app-coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: flutter_app/coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2

      # Issue #239 AC3: the App Store submission pre-flight matrix is plain
      # ruby over flutter_app/fastlane/appstore_preflight.rb — no gems,
      # runs in under a second on the runner's stock ruby.
      # Issue #289 adds the fastlane guard/preflight suites (android id
      # guard + Play upload pre-flight) — same plain-ruby contract, so the
      # step loops over every fastlane test file. Shard 0 only: once is
      # enough (fa PR #333).
      - name: Fastlane pre-flight suites (ruby)
        if: matrix.shard == 0
        run: |
          for t in flutter_app/fastlane/test/*_test.rb; do
            echo "::group::ruby $t"
            ruby "$t"
            echo "::endgroup::"
          done

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Issue #1267 N1 — the macOS exclusion-zone leg. By #177 design the ubuntu
  # PR leg never EXERCISES the JS-engine suites: flutter_app/test/apps/**
  # skip their engine-dependent tests on ubuntu (native_test_guard.dart
  # finds no QuickJS .so on a bare runner), so that surface ran only in the
  # nightly macOS leg — the hole #1309 escaped through (gh-1307: an
  # apps/engine regression merged green and went red the same night).
  #
  # Trigger model (issue #1267 N1 slice 2): ci.yml has NO pull_request
  # trigger — PR validation arrives as an SM workflow_dispatch on the head
  # SHA (machine-sm.yml). The changes classifier derives the validated diff
  # under BOTH events (merge-base(origin/main, HEAD) on dispatches), so
  # this leg is PATH-TRIGGERED: a PR touching only lib/src core never pays
  # for it (AC1), a lib/apps + js_ext diff does, and a classifier failure
  # fails safe (the leg runs). Main/tag/schedule/release runs skip it —
  # gh-1538 retired the nightly flutter-app-macos full-suite backstop
  # (nightly is builds + integration-only now), so this pre-merge leg is
  # the macOS coverage for the JS-engine surface.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  flutter-app-exzone:
    name: Exclusion zone (macOS JS-engine tests)
    runs-on: macos-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') &&
      needs.changes.outputs.exzone == 'true' &&
      needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 25
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      # Pinned stable channel, same as the retired nightly
      # flutter-app-macos leg used (gh-1538).
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF
      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get
      # The guard resolves true on macOS (JavaScriptCore), so the
      # engine-dependent tests RUN here instead of skipping as on ubuntu.
      - name: flutter test test/apps (JS engine live)
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: flutter test --exclude-tags integration test/apps

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Issue #1267 N2 (AC2) — lockfile-modified release smoke. Resolution
  # floats transitive deps to latest-compatible on every resolve, and the
  # breaking arrival (#1265: a transitive flutter_inappwebview nobody
  # declares) lands as a flutter_app/pubspec.lock diff — a surface the PR
  # legs never built: the native linux/windows desktop targets were
  # nightly-only (nightly.yml build-release), so the break surfaced as the
  # 5-red-nights window instead of a red PR. When the diff MODIFIES the
  # lockfile, this matrix release-builds the app on linux+windows pre-merge
  # (the same two targets the nightly carries); every other PR pays
  # nothing. The resolve rides the shared composite action (--enforce-
  # lockfile, #726 retry, skew fail-fast — test/ci_pub_get_retry_guard_
  # test.dart), so a pubspec/lockfile skew fails HERE loudly before any
  # build step. Path-triggered like exzone: pull_request events AND SM
  # validation dispatches (merge-base diff in the classifier, fail-safe).
  # Main/tag/schedule/release runs skip it — the nightly build-release
  # matrix stays the backstop, and a red leg reddens the required Quality
  # gate (platform class — it must block the merge, never the pure-Dart
  # publish, #1368).
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  flutter-app-lock-smoke:
    name: Lockfile smoke (${{ matrix.os }} release)
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') &&
      needs.changes.outputs.locksmoke == 'true' &&
      needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - os: linux
            runner: ubuntu-latest
          - os: windows
            runner: windows-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Same pinned SDK as the nightly build-release legs (#281).
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      # Linux desktop toolchain + plugin native deps (gtk3 for the runner,
      # gstreamer for audioplayers_linux) — same as the nightly linux leg.
      - name: Install Linux desktop toolchain
        if: matrix.os == 'linux'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y clang cmake ninja-build pkg-config \
            libgtk-3-dev liblzma-dev libstdc++-12-dev \
            libgstreamer1.0-dev libgstreamer-plugins-base1.0-dev

      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - name: Create placeholder firebase_options.dart
        shell: bash
        run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      - name: flutter build ${{ matrix.os }} --release (lockfile smoke)
        working-directory: flutter_app
        shell: bash
        run: flutter build ${{ matrix.os }} --release

  # Issue #433: flutter_app CRAP ratchet — the app's beasts were never
  # gated (the root crap4dart.yaml covers core lib/bin only). The 2
  # flutter-tests shards above now emit --coverage; this job merges them
  # into ONE lcov (union DA hits, never cat — same as the core guards)
  # and runs the pinned crap4dart against flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
  # It is also the only home of the config guards: badge sync (AC1),
  # generated-exclude parity (E1) and the only-down git-history threshold
  # guard (AC3) — a raised threshold cannot merge, a new one (bootstrap)
  # can.
  app-crap-gate:
    name: Flutter app CRAP ratchet
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes, flutter-tests]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 6
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: echo "no app/shared changes — flutter_app CRAP green-skipped (required context reported)"
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # only-down guard diffs thresholds against the base
          # gh-1477: blobless — historical blobs are never read.
          filter: blob:none
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - name: Pub cache (crap4dart)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-crap4dart-${{ runner.os }}
          restore-keys: pub-crap4dart-${{ runner.os }}-
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          pattern: app-coverage-shard-*
          path: app-coverage-shards
      - name: Merge shard coverage (union DA hits per file, NOT cat)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          count=$(ls app-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
          if [ "$count" != "2" ]; then
            echo "::error::expected 2 app shard coverage reports, got $count"
            exit 1
          fi
          mkdir -p flutter_app/coverage
          python3 scripts/merge_lcov.py -o flutter_app/coverage/lcov.info \
            app-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info
      - name: Config guards — badge sync, exclude parity, only-down (AC1/E1/AC3)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          BASE_SHA="${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}"
          [ -n "$BASE_SHA" ] || BASE_SHA=HEAD~1
          python3 scripts/check_crap_guards.py --only-down "$BASE_SHA"
      - name: CRAP ratchet (threshold pinned in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          # Issue #447: pin bumped 0.2.1 → >=0.9.5 for the gate framework.
          # gh-1061: >=0.10.0 (analyzer 14.4 refresh).
          # gh-1106: >=0.11.0 <0.12.0 — same bounded pin as the core job;
          # 0.11.0 carries the Type-2 duplication gate the repo pins to.
          # coverage.run_tests: false in both configs — the merged shard
          # lcov above is the source; never re-run the suite here.
          dart pub global activate crap4dart ">=0.11.0 <0.12.0"
          cd flutter_app && dart pub global run crap4dart analyze --format json > crap_report.json

      # Issue #490 AC2: publish the ranked CRAP JSON even when the ratchet
      # is red (analyze writes the report to stdout before its non-zero
      # exit) — descents rank from this artifact, never from a local
      # ad-hoc run.
      - name: Upload crap_report.json artifact (issue 490 AC2)
        if: always() && (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: crap_report
          path: flutter_app/crap_report.json
          retention-days: 30

      - name: Pixel and flutter gates over test/golden/goldens (issue 447)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: cd flutter_app && dart pub global run crap4dart check

  # Issue #283: fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by the test-core template — a
  # duration-balanced manifest (scripts/faui_test_shards.json, rebalanced
  # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml), one file executed by exactly ONE shard,
  # goldens excluded exactly as before (host-locked). Shards fan out INSIDE
  # the job graph; only the aggregate Quality gate is a required check, so
  # a red shard = red gate and path-skipped = neutral (AC4 semantics). A
  # single failed matrix leg can be rerun alone via "Re-run failed jobs"
  # (E1) — the gate then re-aggregates the same results.
  test-faui:
    name: fa_ui tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 12
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      # Shard-manifest assert (AC1/E4): union of the 3 selections == the
      # full non-golden suite, pairwise disjoint, ZERO golden leakage —
      # fails loudly on manifest drift or a golden-pattern rename before
      # any test runs. Pure python, no flutter needed.
      - name: Assert shard manifest (union/disjoint/no-goldens)
        working-directory: packages/fa_ui
        run: >-
          python3 ../../scripts/assert_shard_manifest.py
          ../../scripts/faui_test_shards.json --shards 3 --exclude golden

      - run: cd packages/fa_ui && flutter pub get

      # E2: a NEW test file added by a PR needs no manifest edit —
      # shard_files.py bin-packs uncovered files into shards at runtime;
      # the weekly rebalance then absorbs them into the manifest.
      - name: flutter test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
        working-directory: packages/fa_ui
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 ../../scripts/shard_files.py \
            ../../scripts/faui_test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }} --exclude golden)
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          flutter test --exclude-tags integration --coverage \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/flutter-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 ../../scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/flutter-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-faui-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: faui-coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: packages/fa_ui/coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2

      # junit durations for the weekly shard-rebalance.yml (AC3), same
      # contract as the core shards.
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: junit-faui-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: packages/fa_ui/test-results/junit-faui-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
          retention-days: 7

  # E3/AC6: the 3 shard reports merge into ONE lcov (union DA hits, never
  # cat — no triple-counting). fa_ui coverage is NOT fed into the 80%
  # ratchet: the coverage gate's semantics stay exactly as before; this
  # merged report is telemetry/evidence only.
  faui-coverage:
    name: fa_ui coverage merge (one report)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes, test-faui]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          pattern: faui-coverage-shard-*
          path: faui-coverage-shards

      - name: Merge shard coverage (union DA hits per file, NOT cat)
        run: |
          count=$(ls faui-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
          if [ "$count" != "3" ]; then
            echo "::error::expected 3 fa_ui shard coverage reports, got $count"
            exit 1
          fi
          mkdir -p packages/fa_ui/coverage
          python3 scripts/merge_lcov.py \
            -o packages/fa_ui/coverage/lcov.merged.info \
            faui-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: faui-coverage
          path: packages/fa_ui/coverage/lcov.merged.info
          retention-days: 14

  # Aggregate required check: branch protection requires ONE stable context.
  # Skipped legs (path-filtered out) count as pass — a docs PR must go green
  # on static alone.
  # gh-1005: pinned to hosted linux arm64 alongside pty-visual — same
  # platform-independence evidence (buffer/screen-text assertions, bundled
  # JetBrainsMono, openpty PTYs); PTY screenshots need no macOS, hosted or
  # self-hosted.
  cli-visual-settings:
    name: Settings screenshots (PTY)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # arm64 git bootstrap (no official linux-arm64 Flutter tarball) — same
      # as the flutter-tests and pty-visual legs.
      - name: Flutter SDK (arm64 git bootstrap)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          git clone --depth 1 -b stable https://github.com/flutter/flutter.git "$HOME/flutter"
          echo "$HOME/flutter/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          export PATH="$HOME/flutter/bin:$PATH"
          flutter --version
          flutter precache
      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-

      # gh-1538: the nightly cli-visual job is retired (this PR leg runs the
      # same suite pre-merge) — placeholder rationale lives with the
      # flutter-tests leg.
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: touch .env

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # The harness spawns `dart bin/fah.dart` FROM THE REPO ROOT; without
      # a root package config that resolves package:flutter_agent_harness
      # to the pub-cache copy (an old published build) and the CLI dies on
      # compile errors before the first frame. flutter_app's pub get only
      # writes flutter_app/.dart_tool — the root needs its own.
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: flutter test cli_visual (settings hub flows only)
        run: >-
          cd flutter_app && flutter test test/cli_visual/fa_cli_visual_test.dart
          --tags integration --name "settings hub → (compaction|memory)"

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: cli-visual-settings-screenshots
          path: test/integration/screenshots/
          retention-days: 7

  # Aggregate required check: branch protection requires ONE stable context.
  # Skipped legs (path-filtered out) count as pass — a docs PR must go green
  # on static alone.

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Issue #280: PR-level BUILD verification. The gates above analyze and
  # test but never COMPILE a platform target — a PR could go green while
  # breaking the iOS/macOS/Android/web build (pod/entitlement drift,

  # E4: both macOS legs use GitHub-hosted macos-latest — every job gets its
  # own ephemeral VM, so ios+macos are never serialized on one runner (and

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  build-web:
    name: Build web (debug)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Pinned to the same SDK as the release path (#281): 3.47.x. The

      - name: Create placeholder .env asset

# gh-1625: [INFRA] ci.yml double-fires the full quality gate on release tags (push v* + release published) — dedupe the release-event run to binaries-only

## Description

## Symptom

Tag `v1.0.580` produced **two CI runs** (2026-10-15 05:29Z):

- run 38687023638 — `CI`, event **push**, ref v1.0.580 — in_progress (the full quality gate, by design: gate the tag before anything publishes)
- run 38687023803 — `CI`, event **release**, ref v1.0.580 — pending (the SAME full quality gate again)

Policy (owner): CI runs **once**, pre-merge (via the SM); no double runs on tags, main, or releases. Main-push CI is already retired (gh-1537) and PR CI is dispatch-only — but the **tag double-fire is still there**, and it doubles the release wall time on the exact artifact we ship.

## Why it happens

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` has two triggers that legitimately fire on one release:

1. `push: tags: ['v*']` — the release pipeline keys on the tag; the full quality gate runs on the tag BEFORE anything publishes (gh-1537/gh-1172 design).
2. `release: types: [published]` — added to build + attach the binaries matrix when a release is created (web UI / API / auto-release).

The file's own comment acknowledges the collision: "Pushed tags also arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins)." — i.e. only the **binaries upload** was made idempotent, but the **entire quality matrix re-runs** on the release event. The schedule tick has a `release-pending` pre-check short-circuit; the release event has nothing.

## Fix direction

Dedupe the release-event run, keep its reason to exist:

- **Pre-check job** (`release-dedupe`, mirrors the `release-pending` pattern): runs only on `github.event_name == 'release'`. It checks whether a CI run for the same tag ref (or head SHA) already exists from the `push` event (`gh run list --branch <tag> --event push`, within a recent window).
  - exists (any status) → output `dedupe=true`; the release run **skips every quality leg** (static/test/coverage/guards/flutter) and executes **only the binaries-attach leg** (idempotent `--clobber`, last-wins as today). Fast, seconds-to-minutes.
  - not exists (release cut on an OLD tag, no fresh push) → `dedupe=false`; the release run executes the full gate as today — that path stays the safety net.
- Quality legs get `needs: [release-dedupe]` + `if: needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'` (no-op on push/dispatch/schedule events).
- Keep the documented "tag runs are never cancelled mid-flight" concurrency rule untouched.

## Acceptance

- **AC1** — annotated tag push → release published: exactly ONE full-gate run (the push run); the release run short-circuits to binaries-attach. Two workflow runs may still appear, but the second runs no quality legs.
- **AC2** — release published on an existing old tag (no fresh push): full gate still runs (dedupe=false path).
- **AC3** — push/dispatch/schedule behavior unchanged (PR SM validation, nightly, dry-run arms).
- **AC4** — no race window where BOTH runs attach different binaries: the `--clobber` last-wins semantics preserved and covered by a dry-run log assertion or workflow-lint check.
- **AC5** — the dedupe pre-check fails safe: on `gh run list` API error it outputs `dedupe=false` (full gate runs) rather than skipping blindly.

## Regression guard

A workflow-lint/CI-selftest assertion (aab-gate-selftest pattern) asserting the release-event path short-circuits when a push-run exists for the tag.

Refs: #1522, #1551 (schedule arming), gh-1537 (main-run retirement), gh-1172 (release dispatch).

Assignee: ai-teammate.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

blocks.text:
# Runner split (gh-1005, 2026-09-30): pure-Dart AND all PTY/terminal jobs ->
# ubuntu-24.04-arm (public repo: free, SEPARATE capacity pool from the x64
# queue). Flutter-test legs on arm64 bootstrap the SDK via git clone — Flutter
# ships NO official linux-arm64 SDK (stable manifest is x64 only;
# subosito/flutter-action fails 'version: any architecture: arm64'); x64
# Flutter jobs keep the action. The self-hosted M5 pool is ONE runner
# (fa-m5-1, user LaunchAgent) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work:
# cube-kernel-live. PR PTY legs (integration shards, coverage/duration gates,
# Terminal visual) run hosted-Linux only and never wait on fa-m5-1.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    # gh-1537: NO `branches: [main]` here — the post-merge main CI run is
    # retired. The SM's pre-merge validation dispatch (machine-sm.yml ->
    # factory-sm, strictly serialized) validates the exact tree that
    # merges, so a main-push run would be pure repetition; retiring it
    # kills the duplicate wall time AND the release-bot-commit churn that
    # retriggered it (#1522 lands the tag-sourced versions). The v* tag
    # push stays: the release pipeline (publish/binaries) keys on it, and
    # the full quality gate runs on the tag BEFORE anything publishes.
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (cuts the annotated tag + GitHub Release directly, gh-1522) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the
  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    # gh-1551: the schedule tick IS the release arming mechanism (gh-1537
    # retired the post-merge main run) — but a tick with zero commits on
    # main since the last v* tag has nothing to release, so the
    # `release-pending` pre-check job short-circuits the whole quality
    # gate in seconds (every leg shows SKIPPED explicitly, the run stays
    # green — never a silent absence, never 35-40 min for an empty tick).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Tag/schedule
# runs are never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)

  # FAH_PROVIDER, which used to decide test fate through the args resolver.
  # Run the non-integration suite under the same hostile env so any
  # ambient-env read that leaks back into resolution regresses loudly.
  # gh-1198 rework: the runner now ALSO exports FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE (the
  # provider-queue env won over the file queue and silently flipped the
  # /providers queue editor tests to the env-wins refusal on the PR head) —
  # the var rides the same hostile block so a future ambient read of it
  # regresses here, not only on the runner.
  hostile-env:
    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai
      FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: '{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnvVar":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}'
      FAH_PROVIDER: zai
      FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE: '[{"provider_type":"zai","provider_config":{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnv":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}}]'

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Native-assets hook cache

          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared

          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: dart test under hostile ambient env
        run: dart test --exclude-tags integration

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  # red on main night after night before anyone looked — the CLI-coverage
  # ratchet (12.07% < 12.17%) and the Terminal-visual PTY suite (five

  # the only Terminal-visual gate any tree ever sees; nightly's remaining
  # legs are a scheduled backstop, not a second merge gate.

  # `--version` smoke), never silently fall back to JIT.

    name: AOT fa binary (compiled once per run, gh-1300)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm

      contents: read

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      # assets hooks here so the shard-side restore is warm.
      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: dart build cli (AOT bundle, same shape install_local.sh ships)
        run: |
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=fa-local

      # Issue #487: cross-module duplication gate (issue body measured 20
      # files shipped as app↔core/fa_ui/browser_ext clones). Runs the SAME
      # stage the pre-commit hook runs — one marker, parity diffable. The
      # app leg matters: most cross-module clones are born on the app side
      # and the CRAP/dup steps above stay core/shared-scoped.
      - name: Cross-module duplication ratchet (issue #487)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true'
        run: scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --stages dupx

      # Issue #135 AC1 evidence: a realistic ~300 MB / 100k-record
      # session (3 branches, image blocks, compaction checkpoints)
      # opens through the windowed storage in bounded time and memory.
      # The timing numbers land in the job log; the bounds assertions
      # make regressions (an accidental full read at open) fail here.
      - name: Windowed-open scale evidence (issue #135 AC1)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          dart run scripts/gen_session_fixture.dart \
            --records 100000 --out /tmp/big-session.jsonl \
            --branches 3 --images --compactions --measure | tee /tmp/ac1.log
          python3 - <<'EOF'
          import re, sys
          log = open('/tmp/ac1.log').read()
          total = int(re.search(r'countRecords: (\d+)', log).group(1))
          resident = int(re.search(r'open\+tail: (\d+)', log).group(1))
          assert total >= 100000, f'unexpected record count {total}'
          # The resident window after open is the tail chunk (200) —
          # a full read at open would report ~100k here.
          assert resident <= 1000, f'open read too much: {resident}'
          print(f'AC1 bounds OK: {total} records, {resident} resident at open')
          EOF

      # Issue #199 evidence: a FULL open of the same fixture through the
      # isolate parse executor matches the inline default (parity asserted
      # in-process), and listing 500 small sessions through the repo's
      # bounded-parallel list stays fast. Bounds are generous CI guards;
      # the real numbers land in the job log for trend tracking.
      - name: Isolate parse + parallel listing evidence (issue #199)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          dart run scripts/gen_session_fixture.dart \
            --records 100000 --out /tmp/big-session.jsonl \
            --branches 3 --images --compactions --measure | tee /tmp/ac199.log
          dart run scripts/gen_session_fixture.dart \
            --list-sessions 500 --out /tmp/sessions-199 | tee /tmp/ac199-list.log
          python3 - <<'EOF'
          import re, sys
          log = open('/tmp/ac199.log').read()
          isolate = int(re.search(r'full-open isolate: (\d+)', log).group(1))
          assert isolate < 120000, f'isolate full-open too slow: {isolate} ms'
          assert 'isolate parity: OK' in log, 'isolate/inline parity mismatch'
          llog = open('/tmp/ac199-list.log').read()
          listed = int(re.search(r'list 500 sessions: (\d+)', llog).group(1))
          assert listed < 5000, f'list of 500 sessions too slow: {listed} ms'
          print(f'AC199 OK: isolate full-open {isolate} ms, '
                f'list 500 sessions {listed} ms')
          EOF

  # analyze → test in one 6-min job): analyze runs in parallel with the
  # sharded test legs, each leg no longer waits for it.
  flutter-analyze:
    name: Flutter app analyze (ubuntu)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 8
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-

      # newer flutter validates assets at pub-get/test-build time, so the
      # placeholders must exist BEFORE flutter pub get. Content mirrors the
      # proven build-macos.yml incantation (bare `touch` produced "No file or
      # variants found for asset: .env" on ubuntu/flutter 3.47.4).
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      # compile (Firebase init is skipped for YOUR_* values at runtime).
      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

    name: Flutter app tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      # bf81411e added GoogleService-Info.plist to the Runner target
      # resources (a hard build input). The real plist is gitignored; the
      # release path writes it from GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64
      # (build-mobile.yml), but PR legs have no such secret — seed a
      # placeholder, same trick as the android leg's placeholder
      # google-services.json. Xcode only copies the file; Firebase reads
      # it at app runtime, never at build time.
      - name: Write placeholder GoogleService-Info.plist (iOS)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > flutter_app/ios/Runner/GoogleService-Info.plist << 'EOF'
          <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
          <!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
          <plist version="1.0">
          <dict>
          	<key>GOOGLE_APP_ID</key>
          	<string>1:000000000000:ios:0000000000000000000000</string>
          	<key>API_KEY</key>
          	<string>AIzaSyA-PLACEHOLDER-KEY-FOR-DEBUG-BUILDS-000000</string>
          	<key>PROJECT_ID</key>
          	<string>fa1-placeholder</string>
          	<key>PROJECT_NUMBER</key>
          	<string>000000000000</string>
          	<key>BUNDLE_ID</key>
          	<string>dev.fa1.app</string>
          	<key>GCM_SENDER_ID</key>
          	<string>000000000000</string>
          	<key>IS_ANALYTICS_ENABLED</key>
          	<false/>
          	<key>IS_CRASHLYTICS_ENABLED</key>
          	<false/>
          </dict>
          </plist>
          EOF
          plutil -lint flutter_app/ios/Runner/GoogleService-Info.plist

      # E2: pods cache keyed on Podfile.lock AND a weekly-rolled epoch, so
      # CocoaPods spec drift is re-verified at least weekly even when the
      # lockfile is unchanged. restore-keys falls back to last week's
      # same-lock cache (never a cross-lock cache).
      - name: Compute weekly pods-cache epoch
        id: week
        run: echo "epoch=$(date -u +%Y-W%V)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Cache CocoaPods (iOS)
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: flutter_app/ios/Pods
          key: ios-pods-ci-v1-${{ hashFiles('flutter_app/ios/Podfile.lock') }}-${{ steps.week.outputs.epoch }}
          restore-keys: |
            ios-pods-ci-v1-${{ hashFiles('flutter_app/ios/Podfile.lock') }}-

      - name: Restore vendored WasmRun iOS framework
        timeout-minutes: 15
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The prebuilt XCFramework is excluded from git (the release path
          # prefers the self-hosted runner's local copy; GitHub-hosted PR
          # legs always take the pinned upstream fallback).
          DEST="vendor/wasm_run_flutter/ios/Frameworks"
          rm -rf "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework"
          mkdir -p "$DEST"
          # --retry alone skips transient mid-transfer resets (curl 56).
          curl -L --retry 3 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 10 --max-time 600 \
            -o /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip \
            https://github.com/juancastillo0/wasm_run/releases/download/wasm_run-v0.1.0/WasmRun.xcframework.zip
          unzip -q /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip -d "$DEST"
          ls -la "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework"

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      - name: flutter build ios (debug, unsigned)
        # E2, corrected by gh-1296: classify the failure by EVIDENCE in the
        # log, not by a blanket keyword. The old grep matched 'cocoapods' or
        # 'pod install' in EVERY flutter iOS build log ("Running pod
        # install… 4.4s" prints even on green builds), so every failure was
        # mislabeled "CocoaPods layer — likely spec drift" — that
        # mislabeling sent gh-1296 at a Podfile.lock fix while the real
        # killer was a package build hook (sqlite3's native-assets download
        # hash check). Most-specific layer first; unmatched failures stay
        # unlabeled rather than guessed.
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          cd flutter_app
          if ! flutter build ios --debug --no-codesign 2>&1 | tee /tmp/build-ios.log; then
            if grep -qE 'Building native assets failed|build_hooks failed|Hash of downloaded file|build\.dart returned with exit code' /tmp/build-ios.log; then
              if grep -q 'Hash of downloaded file' /tmp/build-ios.log; then
                echo "::error::iOS build failed in the NATIVE-ASSETS layer: a package build hook downloaded a prebuilt artifact whose SHA-256 no longer matches the hash pinned in the package (upstream re-uploaded a release asset, gh-1296). NOT a CocoaPods/Podfile problem. It self-heals when upstream restores the asset — or bump the package version. The hook's 'To reproduce run:' line above names the package; check its GitHub releases. Raw log above."
              else
                echo "::error::iOS build failed in the NATIVE-ASSETS layer: a package build hook (hook/build.dart) failed. The log names the package and its 'To reproduce run:' line — reproduce locally. NOT a CocoaPods/Podfile problem. Raw log above."
              fi
            elif grep -qE "CocoaPods could not find compatible versions|The sandbox is not in sync with the Podfile\.lock|No podspec found|Error running pod install|Unable to satisfy the following requirements" /tmp/build-ios.log; then
              echo "::error::iOS build failed in the CocoaPods layer — spec/sandbox drift. Fix: cd flutter_app/ios && pod install --repo-update, commit the regenerated Podfile.lock (the pods cache re-rolls weekly, see the cache step; scripts/check_lockfiles.sh pod-sync catches this class pre-merge). Raw log above."
            else
              echo "::error::iOS build failed (Xcode/app layer — no CocoaPods or native-assets signature in the log; read the first error above)."
            fi
            exit 1
          fi

  build-macos:

      - name: Compute weekly pods-cache epoch

      - name: Cache CocoaPods (macOS)
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:

      - name: Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      - name: Ensure flutter_gemma macOS companion dylibs

          if [ -f "$GEMMA_CACHE/libGemmaModelConstraintProvider.dylib" ]; then
            echo "companion dylibs already cached"

            mkdir -p "$GEMMA_CACHE"

              https://github.com/DenisovAV/flutter_gemma/releases/download/native-v0.16.0/litertlm-macos_arm64.tar.gz
            echo "c597554a7a5cdf099658227099a54ef4916c5802b9182757e656e1788f9426b6  /tmp/litertlm-macos_arm64.tar.gz" | shasum -a 256 -c -
            tar xzf /tmp/litertlm-macos_arm64.tar.gz -C "$GEMMA_CACHE"
