              echo "::error::macOS build failed in the CocoaPods layer — likely spec drift. Fix: cd flutter_app/macos && pod install --repo-update, commit the regenerated Podfile.lock (the pods cache re-rolls weekly, see the cache step). Raw log above."
            fi
            exit 1
          fi

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # SEC-08 (#796): CI supply-chain gate. Runs on EVERY PR — no path gating,
  # a security gate you can dodge with a cunning diff is not a gate.
  supply-chain:
    name: Supply-chain gate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Known limit: pull_request/dispatched runs execute THIS file and the
      # checker from the PR's own head — a PR can edit the gate in the same
      # diff. Backstops: reviewers see workflow edits, Dependabot PRs
      # re-verify via their own SM validation dispatch (gh-1537 retired the
      # post-merge main run; there is no longer a scheduled main re-check —
      # nightly.yml is the supervised whole-tree backstop), and
      # sm-merge-guard.yml alarms if a tree lands on main without a
      # successful dispatched validation. A hard guarantee needs a separate
      # workflow_call gate
      # pinned by SHA, invoked from a caller that never comes from the PR
      # (follow-up issue, not this PR).

      # AC1: zero mutable third-party action refs (script + CI job).
      - name: AC1 — all third-party actions SHA-pinned
        run: bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh

      # AC2: every workflow declares an explicit top-level permissions block.
      - name: AC2 — every workflow declares top-level permissions
        run: |
          status=0
          shopt -s nullglob
          for f in .github/workflows/*.yml .github/workflows/*.yaml; do
            [ -f "$f" ] || continue
            if ! grep -q '^permissions:' "$f"; then
              echo "::error file=$f::missing top-level permissions: block"
              status=1
            fi
          done
          exit $status

      # AC4 (REG): the checker must reject a @v4 fixture, a 40-char NON-hex
      # ref (mutable branch with a SHA-shaped name), and a nested composite
      # action manifest — and accept clean equivalents. A gate that cannot
      # fail is decoration.
      - name: AC4 — pin-checker fixture regression
        run: |
          tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
          trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$tmp/bad" "$tmp/bad-hex" "$tmp/bad-composite/.github/actions/probe/deep" "$tmp/bad-awf-ref" "$tmp/bad-other-main" "$tmp/good" "$tmp/good-awf-main" "$tmp/good-composite/.github/actions/probe/deep" "$tmp/string-safe"
          printf 'jobs:\n  probe:\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@v4\n' > "$tmp/bad/bad.yml"
          printf 'jobs:\n  probe:\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@gggggggggggggggggggggggggggggggggggggggg\n' > "$tmp/bad-hex/bad.yml"
          printf 'jobs:\n  probe:\n    steps:\n      - uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@master\n' > "$tmp/bad-awf-ref/wf.yml"
          printf 'jobs:\n  probe:\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@main\n' > "$tmp/bad-other-main/wf.yml"
          printf 'name: probe\nruns:\n  using: composite\n  steps:\n    - uses: actions/checkout@v4\n' > "$tmp/bad-composite/.github/actions/probe/deep/action.yaml"
          printf 'jobs:\n  probe:\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v4\n' > "$tmp/good/good.yml"
          # owner directive 2026-10-04: awf@main is the ONE accepted mutable
          # ref (always-latest, review-gated; per-stub-enforced by
          # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart). Every other
          # mutable ref — awf at a non-main ref, another repo at main —
          # stays a violation (fixtures above).
          printf 'jobs:\n  probe:\n    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@main\n' > "$tmp/good-awf-main/wf.yml"
          printf 'name: probe\nruns:\n  using: composite\n  steps:\n    - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v4\n' > "$tmp/good-composite/.github/actions/probe/deep/action.yaml"
          # String-safety: a uses-shaped string INSIDE a run: scalar is not a
          # step ref — the checker is line-anchored (^[[:space:]]*(- )?uses:)
          # and must not flag it. (Regression: a reviewer suspected the
          # fixture printf lines in this very workflow would trip AC1.)
          printf "jobs:\n  probe:\n    steps:\n      - name: write fixture\n        run: |\n          printf 'jobs:\\\\n  probe:\\\\n    steps:\\\\n      - uses: actions/checkout@v4\\\\n' > out.yml\n          bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh --path . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true\n" > "$tmp/string-safe/wf.yml"
          for bad in bad bad-hex bad-composite bad-awf-ref bad-other-main; do
            if bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh --path "$tmp/$bad" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              echo "::error::pin checker FAILED to flag the $bad fixture"
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh --path "$tmp/good" >/dev/null
          bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh --path "$tmp/good-awf-main" >/dev/null
          bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh --path "$tmp/good-composite" >/dev/null
          bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh --path "$tmp/string-safe" >/dev/null
          echo "fixture regression OK: @v4 / 40-char non-hex / unpinned nested composite / awf@master / other-repo@main rejected; SHA-pinned + awf@main accepted; uses-shaped run-scalar strings ignored"

  # SEC-08 (#796): audit BOTH dependency graphs. pubspec_overrides.yaml
  # redirects dart_tui to the vendored fork (vendor/dart_tui) for local/CI/
  # release builds while pubspec.yaml pins hosted dart_tui for the published
  # package — two different graphs; an audit of one says nothing about the
  # other. Each graph gets its own matrix leg and the split is documented in
  # the audit output.
  dep-audit:
    name: Dependency audit (${{ matrix.graph }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        graph: [hosted, vendored]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      # Hosted leg = exactly what pub.dev consumers resolve; the overrides
      # file never ships, so it must not bend this graph.
      - name: Park vendored overrides (hosted leg)
        if: matrix.graph == 'hosted'
        run: |
          [ -f pubspec_overrides.yaml ] || {
            echo "::error::pubspec_overrides.yaml missing — hosted-leg precondition broke, parking nothing would bend the graph silently"
            exit 1
          }
          mv pubspec_overrides.yaml pubspec_overrides.yaml.vendored
      - run: dart pub get
      - name: Audit the ${{ matrix.graph }} dependency graph
        env:
          GRAPH: ${{ matrix.graph }}
        run: |
          {
            echo "### Dependency audit — \`${GRAPH}\` graph"
            echo ""
            echo "This repo resolves TWO dependency graphs (SEC-08):"
            echo "- **hosted** — \`pubspec.yaml\` alone: what \`pub publish\` ships and pub.dev consumers resolve (dart_tui hosted)."
            echo "- **vendored** — \`pubspec.yaml\` + \`pubspec_overrides.yaml\`: local dev, CI and the release binaries (dart_tui rides \`vendor/dart_tui\`)."
            echo ""
            echo "An audit of one says nothing about the other, so both are audited on every run. Resolved graph:"
            echo ""
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          dart pub deps --style=compact | tee /tmp/graph.txt >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY" || true
          {
            echo ""
            echo "Outdated direct dependencies (informational):"
            echo '```'
            dart pub outdated
            echo '```'
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY" || true
          # The split must be REAL: each leg resolves dart_tui from its own
          # source, read from the resolved pubspec.lock. The block runs from
          # the `dart_tui:` entry header to the next top-level entry header
          # (two-space indent) — no fixed line window to rot.
          lock_block=$(awk 'f && /^  [A-Za-z0-9_.-]+:$/ { exit } /^  dart_tui:$/ { f = 1 } f { print }' pubspec.lock)
          # Vacuous-assertion guard: if dart_tui ever leaves the lock (or
          # the entry is renamed) the block is empty and the per-graph
          # greps below would fail bare (exit 1, no annotation) or — worse
          # for future shape changes — pass on nothing. Fail loudly here.
          [ -n "$lock_block" ] || {
            echo "::error::no dart_tui entry found in pubspec.lock — the audit assertion is vacuous, aborting"
            exit 1
          }
          echo "$lock_block"
          case "$GRAPH" in
            hosted)
              if echo "$lock_block" | grep -q 'source: path'; then
                echo "::error::hosted graph resolved the vendored dart_tui fork"
                exit 1
              fi
              echo "$lock_block" | grep -q 'source: hosted'
              ;;
            vendored)
              echo "$lock_block" | grep -q 'source: path' || {
                echo "::error::vendored graph did not resolve dart_tui from vendor/dart_tui"
                exit 1
              }
              ;;
          esac
          echo "$GRAPH graph audit OK"

      # gh-1248 (review): the vendored fork has its own test suite, but no
      # root-level `dart test` ever discovers it — the fork's tests can rot
      # invisibly (that is exactly how the gh-1248 regression suite shipped
      # with a compile error). Run analyze + tests on the vendored leg,
      # where pubspec_overrides.yaml resolves the fork in-place.
      - name: Vendor fork tests (dart_tui)
        if: matrix.graph == 'vendored'
        run: |
          cd vendor/dart_tui
          dart pub get
          # Vendored third-party code: analyze keeps ERRORS fatal (the
          # gh-1248 compile rot this step exists to catch was error-level)
          # but pre-existing vendor warnings must not red unrelated PRs.
          # Plain `dart analyze` has no --no-fatal-infos (that flag is the
          # flutter tool's; infos are already non-fatal by default) — only
          # warnings need negating here. The test run below is the fatal gate.
          dart analyze --no-fatal-warnings
          dart test

  # SEC-07 (#795) AC4: run the installer against fixture releases
  # (good / tampered / unsigned) on EVERY PR — no path gating needed at
  # ~15s/job, and a security IT you can dodge with a cunning diff is not
  # an IT. macOS leg exercises the real quarantine-strip ordering (AC3).
  installer-verify:
    name: Installer verify IT (${{ matrix.os }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Installer verification fixtures (AC1-AC4)
        run: bash scripts/installer_verify_selftest.sh

  # SEC-07 follow-up (#1015 incident): the release install.sh pins by default
  # must itself carry signed provenance — otherwise a fresh curl|sh refuses
  # the installer's own default with E_PIN_PROVENANCE_MISSING. Runs the pin
  # gate live (network to github.com releases, read-only) on EVERY PR — no
  # path gating, same reasoning as installer-verify. Fixture coverage of the
  # gate's failure modes lives in installer-verify (contract 5).
  install-pin-gate:
    name: Install pin provenance gate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Pinned release must carry signed provenance
        run: bash scripts/check_install_pin.sh

  quality-gate:
    name: Quality gate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes, static, flutter-analyze, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, perf-gate, usage-fold, cli-visual-settings, cube-kernel-live, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos, integration-mock, hostile-env, fa-aot-build, pty-integration-linux, pty-coverage-gate, pty-visual, supply-chain, dep-audit, installer-portability, installer-verify, install-pin-gate, flutter-app-exzone, flutter-app-lock-smoke]
    if: always() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    # #1368: the publish job consumes dart_ok — the pure-Dart package verdict
    # — instead of this aggregate's result. The aggregate itself stays the
    # single required check: any red leg (platform included) still fails it.
    outputs:
      dart_ok: ${{ steps.gate.outputs.dart_ok }}
    steps:
      - name: Report leg results
        run: |
          echo "static        = ${{ needs.static.result }}"
          echo "hostile-env   = ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"
          echo "test-core     = ${{ needs.test-core.result }}"
          echo "coverage-gate = ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}"
          echo "guards        = ${{ needs.guards.result }}"
          echo "flutter-analyze = ${{ needs.flutter-analyze.result }}"
          echo "flutter-tests = ${{ needs.flutter-tests.result }}"
          echo "test-faui     = ${{ needs.test-faui.result }}"
          echo "app-crap-gate = ${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}"
          echo "perf-gate     = ${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}"
          echo "usage-fold    = ${{ needs.usage-fold.result }}"
          echo "cube-live     = ${{ needs.cube-kernel-live.result }}"
          echo "cli-visual    = ${{ needs.cli-visual-settings.result }}"
          echo "build-web     = ${{ needs.build-web.result }}"
          echo "build-android = ${{ needs.build-android.result }}"
          echo "build-ios     = ${{ needs.build-ios.result }}"
          echo "build-macos   = ${{ needs.build-macos.result }}"
          echo "integ-mock    = ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}"
          echo "hostile-env   = ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"
          echo "pty-integ-linux = ${{ needs.pty-integration-linux.result }}"
          echo "fa-aot-build  = ${{ needs.fa-aot-build.result }}"
          echo "pty-gates     = ${{ needs.pty-coverage-gate.result }}"
          echo "pty-visual    = ${{ needs.pty-visual.result }}"
          echo "supply-chain  = ${{ needs.supply-chain.result }}"
          echo "dep-audit     = ${{ needs.dep-audit.result }}"
          echo "installer-it = ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}"
          echo "installer-reg  = ${{ needs.installer-portability.result }}"
          echo "pin-gate    = ${{ needs.install-pin-gate.result }}"
          echo "exzone      = ${{ needs.flutter-app-exzone.result }}"

        env:
          R_CHANGES: ${{ needs.changes.result }}
          R_SUPPLY_CHAIN: ${{ needs.supply-chain.result }}
          R_DEP_AUDIT: ${{ needs.dep-audit.result }}
          R_STATIC: ${{ needs.static.result }}
          R_FLUTTER_ANALYZE: ${{ needs.flutter-analyze.result }}
          R_TEST_CORE: ${{ needs.test-core.result }}
          R_COVERAGE: ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}
          R_GUARDS: ${{ needs.guards.result }}
          R_FLUTTER: ${{ needs.flutter-tests.result }}
          R_CRAP: ${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}
          R_FAUI: ${{ needs.test-faui.result }}
          R_PERF: ${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}
          R_USAGE_FOLD: ${{ needs.usage-fold.result }}
          R_CUBE: ${{ needs.cube-kernel-live.result }}
          R_CLI_VISUAL: ${{ needs.cli-visual-settings.result }}
          R_BUILD_WEB: ${{ needs.build-web.result }}
          R_BUILD_ANDROID: ${{ needs.build-android.result }}
          R_BUILD_IOS: ${{ needs.build-ios.result }}
          R_BUILD_MACOS: ${{ needs.build-macos.result }}
          R_INTEG: ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}
          R_HOSTILE: ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}
          R_PTY_LINUX: ${{ needs.pty-integration-linux.result }}
          R_FA_AOT: ${{ needs.fa-aot-build.result }}
          R_PTY_GATES: ${{ needs.pty-coverage-gate.result }}
          R_PTY_VISUAL: ${{ needs.pty-visual.result }}
          R_INSTALLER_VERIFY: ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}
          R_INSTALLER_REG: ${{ needs.installer-portability.result }}

          R_EXZONE: ${{ needs.flutter-app-exzone.result }}

          # not a pass — review follow-up, #796/#801.

blocks.text:
# gh-1625: [INFRA] ci.yml double-fires the full quality gate on release tags (push v* + release published) — dedupe the release-event run to binaries-only

## Description

## Symptom

Tag `v1.0.580` produced **two CI runs** (2026-10-15 05:29Z):

- run 38687023638 — `CI`, event **push**, ref v1.0.580 — in_progress (the full quality gate, by design: gate the tag before anything publishes)
- run 38687023803 — `CI`, event **release**, ref v1.0.580 — pending (the SAME full quality gate again)

Policy (owner): CI runs **once**, pre-merge (via the SM); no double runs on tags, main, or releases. Main-push CI is already retired (gh-1537) and PR CI is dispatch-only — but the **tag double-fire is still there**, and it doubles the release wall time on the exact artifact we ship.

## Why it happens

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` has two triggers that legitimately fire on one release:

1. `push: tags: ['v*']` — the release pipeline keys on the tag; the full quality gate runs on the tag BEFORE anything publishes (gh-1537/gh-1172 design).
2. `release: types: [published]` — added to build + attach the binaries matrix when a release is created (web UI / API / auto-release).

The file's own comment acknowledges the collision: "Pushed tags also arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins)." — i.e. only the **binaries upload** was made idempotent, but the **entire quality matrix re-runs** on the release event. The schedule tick has a `release-pending` pre-check short-circuit; the release event has nothing.

## Fix direction

Dedupe the release-event run, keep its reason to exist:

- **Pre-check job** (`release-dedupe`, mirrors the `release-pending` pattern): runs only on `github.event_name == 'release'`. It checks whether a CI run for the same tag ref (or head SHA) already exists from the `push` event (`gh run list --branch <tag> --event push`, within a recent window).
  - exists (any status) → output `dedupe=true`; the release run **skips every quality leg** (static/test/coverage/guards/flutter) and executes **only the binaries-attach leg** (idempotent `--clobber`, last-wins as today). Fast, seconds-to-minutes.
  - not exists (release cut on an OLD tag, no fresh push) → `dedupe=false`; the release run executes the full gate as today — that path stays the safety net.
- Quality legs get `needs: [release-dedupe]` + `if: needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'` (no-op on push/dispatch/schedule events).
- Keep the documented "tag runs are never cancelled mid-flight" concurrency rule untouched.

## Acceptance

- **AC1** — annotated tag push → release published: exactly ONE full-gate run (the push run); the release run short-circuits to binaries-attach. Two workflow runs may still appear, but the second runs no quality legs.
- **AC2** — release published on an existing old tag (no fresh push): full gate still runs (dedupe=false path).
- **AC3** — push/dispatch/schedule behavior unchanged (PR SM validation, nightly, dry-run arms).
- **AC4** — no race window where BOTH runs attach different binaries: the `--clobber` last-wins semantics preserved and covered by a dry-run log assertion or workflow-lint check.
- **AC5** — the dedupe pre-check fails safe: on `gh run list` API error it outputs `dedupe=false` (full gate runs) rather than skipping blindly.

## Regression guard

A workflow-lint/CI-selftest assertion (aab-gate-selftest pattern) asserting the release-event path short-circuits when a push-run exists for the tag.

Refs: #1522, #1551 (schedule arming), gh-1537 (main-run retirement), gh-1172 (release dispatch).

Assignee: ai-teammate.

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside

  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no

  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed

blocks.text:
# Runner split (gh-1005, 2026-09-30): pure-Dart AND all PTY/terminal jobs ->
# ubuntu-24.04-arm (public repo: free, SEPARATE capacity pool from the x64
# queue). Flutter-test legs on arm64 bootstrap the SDK via git clone — Flutter
# ships NO official linux-arm64 SDK (stable manifest is x64 only;
# subosito/flutter-action fails 'version: any architecture: arm64'); x64
# Flutter jobs keep the action. The self-hosted M5 pool is ONE runner
# (fa-m5-1, user LaunchAgent) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work:
# cube-kernel-live. PR PTY legs (integration shards, coverage/duration gates,
# Terminal visual) run hosted-Linux only and never wait on fa-m5-1.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    # gh-1537: NO `branches: [main]` here — the post-merge main CI run is
    # retired. The SM's pre-merge validation dispatch (machine-sm.yml ->
    # factory-sm, strictly serialized) validates the exact tree that
    # merges, so a main-push run would be pure repetition; retiring it
    # kills the duplicate wall time AND the release-bot-commit churn that
    # retriggered it (#1522 lands the tag-sourced versions). The v* tag
    # push stays: the release pipeline (publish/binaries) keys on it, and
    # the full quality gate runs on the tag BEFORE anything publishes.
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (cuts the annotated tag + GitHub Release directly, gh-1522) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the
  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    # gh-1551: the schedule tick IS the release arming mechanism (gh-1537
    # retired the post-merge main run) — but a tick with zero commits on
    # main since the last v* tag has nothing to release, so the
    # `release-pending` pre-check job short-circuits the whole quality
    # gate in seconds (every leg shows SKIPPED explicitly, the run stays
    # green — never a silent absence, never 35-40 min for an empty tick).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Tag/schedule
# runs are never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   installer-portability → gh-1596 REG-1/REG-2: the POSIX-dialect proof
#               for the first-run wizard (site/** or the generator
#               touched) — dash + busybox ash on ubuntu, bash on macOS;
#               red blocks the merge via the quality-gate platform class
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
#   release-pending → gh-1551 empty-tick short-circuit: the schedule is
#                the release arming mechanism (gh-1537), but a tick with
#                no commits since the last v* tag skips the whole gate
#                in seconds (see the job comment below)
# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,
#   integration) are unchanged in semantics — they just need the new aggregate.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal default — every job that needs more
# declares its own job-level permissions block.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # gh-1551: slim the 2h schedule tick. The schedule is the release arming
  # mechanism (gh-1537 retired the post-merge main run), but a tick with
  # ZERO commits on main since the last v* tag has nothing to release —
  # running the full ~35-40 min quality gate for it is pure waste against
  # the shift-left / zero-duplicate-runs principle (observed: run
  # 38147581679, 2026-10-11). This cheap pre-check (~10-30 s: one checkout
  # + git rev-list) compares main HEAD against the latest semver v* tag and
  # exports `pending`; every gate leg ANDs the output into its `if`, so an
  # empty tick short-circuits the whole graph in seconds — legs show
  # SKIPPED explicitly (visible in the run, never silently absent) and the
  # run stays green.
  #
  # Arms that must NEVER be blocked (gh-1551 AC3): v* tag pushes,
  # `release: published` events and both dispatch arms (releaseDryRun /
  # releaseDispatch — incl. every SM validation dispatch, which is a
  # workflow_dispatch on the PR head). All of them short-circuit to
  # pending=true BEFORE the checkout — they do not even pay the fetch, and
  # the gate graph is byte-identical to gh-1537 for them.
  #
  # Fail-open (AC4): `pending` defaults to true and is flipped to false
  # only inside the zero-commits branch — a flaky pre-check (tag fetch
  # hiccup, rev-list error) …

# dmtools ai-teammate runner exports FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG /
  # FAH_PROVIDER, which used to decide test fate through the args resolver.
  # Run the non-integration suite under the same hostile env so any
  # ambient-env read that leaks back into resolution regresses loudly.
  # gh-1198 rework: the runner now ALSO exports FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE (the
  # provider-queue env won over the file queue and silently flipped the
  # /providers queue editor tests to the env-wins refusal on the PR head) —
  # the var rides the same hostile block so a future ambient read of it
  # regresses here, not only on the runner.
  hostile-env:
    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai
      FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: '{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnvVar":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}'
      FAH_PROVIDER: zai
      FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE: '[{"provider_type":"zai","provider_config":{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnv":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}}]'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: dart test under hostile ambient env
        run: dart test --exclude-tags integration

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Nightly parity (2026-09-23): the two legs that stayed nightly-only went
  # red on main night after night before anyone looked — the CLI-coverage
  # ratchet (12.07% < 12.17%) and the Terminal-visual PTY suite (five
  # regressions, several cascading out of fixed-port collisions). Both legs
  # are part of the COMMON PR suite: they run on every CI invocation (the
  # Machine SM dispatches ci.yml per PR head), unconditioned by path — a
  # diff that breaks them must red-block THE PR, never the 3:30 nightly.
  # gh-1538: nightly is builds + integration-only now — this PR leg IS the
  # only Terminal-visual run (the nightly cli-visual duplicate is retired).
  # gh-1537 retired the post-merge main CI run, so this pre-merge leg is
  # the only Terminal-visual gate any tree ever sees; nightly's remaining
  # legs are a scheduled backstop, not a second merge gate.
  # gh-1300 (2026-10-06): the PTY/CLI shards pay toolchain+boot ONCE per
  # run, not per test. Every integration test spawns a fresh CLI; JIT
  # `dart bin/fah.dart` cost VM start + CFE kernel compile ~30 s PER SPAWN
  # on loaded ARM runners (the dominant term: 29 files, 3 shards x
  # ~350 s). This job compiles the AOT bundle once, the shards download
  # it and point the FA_BIN seam (test/integration/pty_harness.dart,
  # faCliCommand) at it — spawn ~1 s, per-test isolation untouched (each
  # spawn is still a fresh process with its own env/cwd). The binary MUST
  # match the PR's sources: built fresh in this run, never cached across
  # runs; the shards fail loudly if it is missing or dead (`test -x` +
  # `--version` smoke), never silently fall back to JIT.
  fa-aot-build:
    name: AOT fa binary (compiled once per run, gh-1300)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: release-pending
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      # Same hooks cache key as the shards: the build pays the native
      # assets hooks here so the shard-side restore is warm.
      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-
      - run: dart pub get
      - name: dart build cli (AOT bundle, same shape install_local.sh ships)
        run: |
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=fa-local
          # The installer writes version.txt into the bundle; mirror it so
          # `fa --version` from the AOT binary reports the real version
          # (the _packageVersion() fallback chain reads bundle/version.txt).
          # gh-1522: the committed pubspec is the 0.0.0-dev placeholder —
          # PR runs stamp from git describe (falls back to the short sha
          # on shallow checkouts); release runs get the exact tag from the
          # release binaries job.
          version=$(git describe --tags --always --dirty 2>/dev/null || echo 0.0.0-dev)
          version="${version#v}"
          echo "$version" > fa-local/bundle/version.txt
          ./fa-local/bundle/bin/fah --version
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: fa-aot-bin
          path: fa-local/bundle/
          retention-days: 1

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  # the whole shard manifest (scripts/test_integration_shards.json) found
  # ZERO genuinely macOS-specific tests: the PTY harness allocates terminals
  # via libc openpty FFI (package:pty2 — OS/arch independent), no suite
  # depends on zsh defaults or /bin/bash 3.2 quirks, and the one macOS-only
  # assertion (fa_cube_integration_test.dart's SBPL kernel nested-rw probe)
  # is `if (Platform.isMacOS)`-guarded inside a test that passes on Linux.
  # The genuinely macOS-only terminal behavior keeps its dedicated gates:
  # cube-kernel-live (above) runs the real sandbox-exec E2E (test/cube/
  # backends) on fa-m5-1, and the mac-only CLI lines (shift_hid CoreGraphics
  # probe, stty -f device flag) stay unit-covered on ubuntu
  # (test/cli/shift_hid_test.dart, fa_tui_controller_overlay_test.dart).
  # Consequence: the fa-m5 runner-pick probe (M5_POOL) is GONE and the mac
  # leg merged INTO the linux leg below — ONE sharded PTY/CLI integration
  # job on ubuntu-24.04-arm that now also carries the per-shard coverage +
  # dart-json/junit reporting the gate consumes. A PR validation's PTY legs
  # never wait on fa-m5-1; hosted macOS (10x minute cost) is never used.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  pty-integration-linux:
    # THE PR PTY/CLI integration leg (gh-1005: the former mac leg merged in;

    # duration-balanced shards — scripts/test_integration_shards.json,
    # file-level units). New integration-tagged files bin-pack in at runtime
    # (shard_files.py --tags integration), so a PR adding one never
    # silently skips it. Explicit --concurrency=4 bounds in-suite
    # parallelism (part 3.3 — package:test forbids `concurrency` in
    # dart_test.yaml tag overrides, so the knob lives here; it bounds
    # concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB — the rate-limit rationale is
    # documented on the llm tag in dart_test.yaml).

sys.exit(0 if float(pct) < 1.0 else 1)
          EOF

      # Issue #487: cross-module duplication gate (issue body measured 20
      # files shipped as app↔core/fa_ui/browser_ext clones). Runs the SAME
      # stage the pre-commit hook runs — one marker, parity diffable. The
      # app leg matters: most cross-module clones are born on the app side
      # and the CRAP/dup steps above stay core/shared-scoped.
      - name: Cross-module duplication ratchet (issue #487)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true'
        run: scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --stages dupx

      # Issue #135 AC1 evidence: a realistic ~300 MB / 100k-record
      # session (3 branches, image blocks, compaction checkpoints)
      # opens through the windowed storage in bounded time and memory.
      # The timing numbers land in the job log; the bounds assertions
      # make regressions (an accidental full read at open) fail here.
      - name: Windowed-open scale evidence (issue #135 AC1)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          dart run scripts/gen_session_fixture.dart \
            --records 100000 --out /tmp/big-session.jsonl \
            --branches 3 --images --compactions --measure | tee /tmp/ac1.log
          python3 - <<'EOF'
          import re, sys
          log = open('/tmp/ac1.log').read()
          total = int(re.search(r'countRecords: (\d+)', log).group(1))
          resident = int(re.search(r'open\+tail: (\d+)', log).group(1))
          assert total >= 100000, f'unexpected record count {total}'
          # The resident window after open is the tail chunk (200) —
          # a full read at open would report ~100k here.
          assert resident <= 1000, f'open read too much: {resident}'
          print(f'AC1 bounds OK: {total} records, {resident} resident at open')
          EOF

      # Issue #199 evidence: a FULL open of the same fixture through the
      # isolate parse executor matches the inline default (parity asserted
      # in-process), and listing 500 small sessions through the repo's
      # bounded-parallel list stays fast. Bounds are generous CI guards;
      # the real numbers land in the job log for trend tracking.
      - name: Isolate parse + parallel listing evidence (issue #199)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          dart run scripts/gen_session_fixture.dart \
            --records 100000 --out /tmp/big-session.jsonl \
            --branches 3 --images --compactions --measure | tee /tmp/ac199.log
          dart run scripts/gen_session_fixture.dart \
            --list-sessions 500 --out /tmp/sessions-199 | tee /tmp/ac199-list.log
          python3 - <<'EOF'
          import re, sys
          log = open('/tmp/ac199.log').read()
          isolate = int(re.search(r'full-open isolate: (\d+)', log).group(1))
          assert isolate < 120000, f'isolate full-open too slow: {isolate} ms'
          assert 'isolate parity: OK' in log, 'isolate/inline parity mismatch'
          llog = open('/tmp/ac199-list.log').read()
          listed = int(re.search(r'list 500 sessions: (\d+)', llog).group(1))
          assert listed < 5000, f'list of 500 sessions too slow: {listed} ms'
          print(f'AC199 OK: isolate full-open {isolate} ms, '
                f'list 500 sessions {listed} ms')
          EOF

          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" > /tmp/jobs.json; then

            fi
            if [ "$attempt" = 3 ]; then
              echo "::error::gh api jobs fetch failed after 3 attempts — GitHub API is erroring (502-class)"

            fi
            echo "::warning::gh api jobs fetch failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"

          print('|---|---|---|---|')

                  t0 = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s['started_at'].replace('Z', '+00:00'))
                  t1 = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s['completed_at'].replace('Z', '+00:00'))
                  print(f"| {j['name']} | {s['name']} | {int((t1 - t0).total_seconds())}s | {s['conclusion']} |")
          EOF
          cp /tmp/jobs.json step-timings.json

  # Issue #194 (point 4): >2x-baseline watchdog. The timeout-minutes above
  # are ≈2x the healthy job durations observed on main (shards 3-5 min,
  # flutter-tests ~6 min + fa_ui shards ~5 min since issue #283). A timeout means this run landed on a degraded
  # runner allocation; the remedy is a fresh EMPTY-COMMIT push — a new run
  # gets a fresh allocation and the push cancels this stale run via the PR
  # concurrency group. NEVER `gh run rerun`: it reallocates into the same
  # degraded pool. One retrigger max per head commit (loop guard below).
  watchdog:
    name: Watchdog (degraded-runner retrigger)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    # pty-integration-linux/pty-visual ride along (review 2026-09-23, #963;
    # gh-1005 retired the mac shards): the longest legs. They must be in
    # `needs` or the watchdog fires before they settle — a degraded-runner
    # timeout there would land after the scan and never get its one-shot
    # empty-commit retrigger. Cost: the watchdog waits for them.
    needs: [changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, test-faui, pty-integration-linux, pty-visual]
    # Same-repo PRs only: the empty-commit retrigger pushes to the PR branch,
    # which this token cannot do for a fork's ref.
    if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Detect a timeout-type failure
        id: trip
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          trip=false
          for id in $(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
              --jq '.jobs[] | select(.conclusion=="failure") | .id'); do
            # A job-level timeout cancels the running step: the job is
            # 'failure' but its LAST step is 'cancelled'. A real test
            # failure ends with a failed step.
            last=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/jobs/$id" --jq '.steps[-1].conclusion // ""')
            echo "job $id last step: $last"
            if [ "$last" = "cancelled" ]; then trip=true; fi
          done
          echo "trip=$trip" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: steps.trip.outputs.trip == 'true'
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger workflows — the retrigger must
          # re-fire CI, so it rides RELEASE_PAT (same as release/gardener).
          token: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}

      - name: Retrigger with an empty commit (fresh runner allocation)
        if: steps.trip.outputs.trip == 'true'
        env:
          HAS_PAT: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT != '' }}
        run: |
          if [ "$HAS_PAT" != "true" ]; then
            echo "::notice::RELEASE_PAT not configured — cannot retrigger"
            exit 0
          fi
          msg="ci: watchdog retrigger (degraded runner pool)"
          if [ "$(git log -1 --format=%s)" = "$msg" ]; then
            echo "head commit is already a watchdog retrigger — not looping"
            exit 0
          fi
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git commit --allow-empty -m "$msg"
          git push origin HEAD:"${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}"
  integration:
    name: Provider smoke (LLM, tag-only)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    # Same !cancelled() pattern as the release/binaries jobs (fa#456).
    # #1368: the gate check reads the dart_ok OUTPUT, not the aggregate
    # result — a platform-only red (Windows build, PTY leg) used to skip this
    # smoke transitively and with it the publish job (the v1.0.519-521
    # starvation). dart_ok=false (a red package leg) still skips it: the
    # publish it gates cannot run anyway.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.outputs.dart_ok != 'false' &&
      github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    env:
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
      GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
      OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      # Issue #551: the ONLY tag-only LLM job — a small provider smoke.
      # `--tags "integration && llm"` selects the real-provider files
      # (anthropic / google / openrouter / ollama round-trips; copilot,
      # chatgpt-codex and subagent-real-model self-skip without their
      # creds). The 50-file integration suite itself runs per-PR now
      # (integration-mock + nightly pty-integration): tag CI no longer
      # gates releases on it, publish waits on this smoke instead.
      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-
      - name: dart test --tags "integration && llm"
        run: dart test --tags "integration && llm"

  js-ext-integration:
    name: JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, quality-gate]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 25
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: Install quickjs-ng
        run: |
          curl -fsSL -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/qjs" \
            https://github.com/quickjs-ng/quickjs/releases/download/v0.16.2/qjs-linux-x86_64
          chmod +x "$RUNNER_TEMP/qjs"
          echo "$RUNNER_TEMP" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
      - name: dart test --tags integration (qjs engine suites)
        run: dart test --tags integration test/cli/ext_engine_process_test.dart test/js_ext/integration/

  publish:
    name: Publish to pub.dev
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [quality-gate, integration]
    # 20m ceiling: publish flow (~2-4m) + the post-upload verify window
    # (11m, #611) must both fit — 10m would kill a healthy poll mid-window.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check — the fa#456 class: GitHub propagates
    # "skipped" TRANSITIVELY through the always()-quality-gate's needs graph.
    #
    # #1368, two changes:
    # 1. PUSH-EVENT TAGS ONLY. pub.dev trusted publishing accepts OIDC tokens
    #    from push and workflow_dispatch events ONLY — there is no
    #    release-event option (owner verified the pub.dev console). The old
    #    release arm made the release-event twin of every tag ATTEMPT the
    #    publish whenever the push twin had not uploaded — pub.dev rejected
    #    the token's event claim and the leg died "Authentication failed!"
    #    (exit 65) on every release since the gate graph grew legs that can
    #    redden the push twin. The v0.1.370-402 era this arm once covered
    #    (API-created lightweight tags with no push event) is gone: every tag
    #    is PAT-pushed annotated (gh-1522: the auto_release.sh App-token tag
    #    push), so the push twin
    #    always exists. A release-only tag would now skip publish and the
    #    daily verifyPubDev leg alarms «only release-event run(s)» loudly.
    # 2. The gate is dart_ok — the pure-Dart package verdict quality-gate
    #    exports — NOT the aggregate result. A red native binary/PTY leg must
    #    never hold a Dart package hostage (v1.0.520's push twin: publish
    #    skipped off a red pty-integration shard). The Provider smoke stays a
    #    hard gate (#551): needs.integration.result == 'success'.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.outputs.dart_ok == 'true' &&
      needs.integration.result == 'success' &&
      github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    concurrency:
      # push + release events both fire for PAT-pushed tags; serialize the
      # double-fire so the loser no-ops on the already-published guard below
      # instead of racing dart pub publish (version already exists → red).
      # #1368: only the push twin can publish now — the group stays as a
      # belt-and-suspenders guard for re-pushed tags.
      group: publish-${{ github.ref }}
      cancel-in-progress: false
    permissions:
      id-token: write # OIDC — pub.dev verifies the GitHub identity, no secrets
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # A tag is a release announcement: if pubspec says publish_to: none,
      # failing LOUDLY is correct (#554) — a green skip is how pub.dev went
      # 35 versions stale unnoticed. Removing the flag from pubspec re-enables.
      - id: gate
        name: Publish gate
        run: |
          if grep -Eq '^publish_to:[[:space:]]*none' pubspec.yaml; then
            echo "::error::pubspec.yaml sets publish_to: none — a tagged release cannot reach pub.dev. Remove the flag from pubspec.yaml, or stop tagging v* releases (see #554)."
            exit 1
          fi
          # gh-1452 + gh-1522: pub.dev server-rejects the upload when the
          # PACKED changelog is at/over its 262144-byte content cap
          # (v1.0.538 died mid-upload). The repo CHANGELOG.md is
          # CURATED-ONLY and is NOT what pub packs — the staged changelog
          # is trimmed under the cap by stamp_staged_release.sh before
          # upload — so an over-cap repo file must never kill the release
          # train (that is the exact #1452 class gh-1522 retired). Warn
          # loudly here; the HARD gate is the staged re-measure ahead of
          # `dart pub publish`.
          if ! bash scripts/check_changelog_size.sh CHANGELOG.md; then
            echo "::warning::CHANGELOG.md is at/over the pub.dev 262144-byte cap — the staged (published) changelog is trimmed to fit, so this release proceeds, but archive the tail to CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md (gh-1452)."
          fi
          echo "publishable=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: steps.gate.outputs.publishable == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      # gh-1522: the repo pubspec carries the 0.0.0-dev placeholder — the
      # tag is the version. Guard the invariant instead of comparing the
      # tag to the placeholder: the committed pubspec must still BE the
      # placeholder (a hand-bump desyncs the tag↔staged-file invariant the
      # stamper relies on), and the staged version must equal the tag.
      - name: Verify committed pubspec carries the placeholder (publish job)
        if: steps.gate.outputs.publishable == 'true'
        run: |
          tag="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
          placeholder=$(grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml | awk '{print $2}')
          if [ "$placeholder" != "0.0.0-dev" ]; then
            echo "::error::committed pubspec.yaml version is '$placeholder', expected the 0.0.0-dev placeholder — the tag is the single source of truth (gh-1522); a hand-bump desyncs the staged stamp. Revert pubspec.yaml."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "tag=$tag placeholder=$placeholder"

      # setup-dart (sdk >= 3.13) provisions a publish-scoped credential for
      # the whole job: it exports PUB_TOKEN and registers
      # `dart pub token add https://pub.dev --env-var PUB_TOKEN`, so EVERY
      # pub.dev request — including `dart pub get` metadata reads — carries
      # the publish token. pub.dev rejects it on metadata reads
      # ("depends on ... which doesn't exist (authorization failed)",
      # exit 69; tag v0.1.340, run 34503923233). Resolution must run
      # unauthenticated: strip the credential, resolve, restore it only
      # for the publish step.
      - name: Strip publish credential for dependency resolution
        if: steps.gate.outputs.publishable == 'true'
        run: dart pub token remove https://pub.dev || true

      - run: dart pub get
        if: steps.gate.outputs.publishable == 'true'

      # The repo root hosts sub-projects that are NOT part of the pub
      # package (flutter_app with its 57 MB wasm toolchain, yoclip media,
      # browser_ext, office_addin, vendored forks, docs) — `dart publish`
      # packs everything under the root that isn't gitignored, which blew
      # the archive past pub.dev's hard 100 MB cap (v0.1.406: 100.4 MB,
      # "Content-length exceeds upper bound"). Publish from a staged copy
      # that carries only the package surface; the size guard makes any
      # future bloat a LOCI error instead of a pub.dev rejection.
      # gh-1522: publish from a staged copy stamped with the TAG version —
      # the staged pubspec version and the generated changelog section are
      # written at stage time (scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh), the repo
      # files keep the 0.0.0-dev placeholder and are never mutated.
      - name: Stage publishable package (sub-projects stay out)
        if: steps.gate.outputs.publishable == 'true'
        run: |
          bash scripts/stage_publish_package.sh /tmp/publish-stage "${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
          (cd /tmp/publish-stage && dart pub get)

      # gh-1522 guard: the staged pubspec version MUST equal the tag name
      # (v1.0.550 → 1.0.550) — fail BEFORE the upload, never mid-publish.
      - name: Verify staged version matches tag
        if: steps.gate.outputs.publishable == 'true'
        run: |
          tag="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
          staged=$(grep '^version:' /tmp/publish-stage/pubspec.yaml | awk '{print $2}')
          echo "tag=$tag staged=$staged"
          if [ "$tag" != "$staged" ]; then
            echo "::error::staged pubspec version $staged does not match tag v$tag — refusing to publish (gh-1522)"
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Publish (automated publishing via OIDC)
        if: steps.gate.outputs.publishable == 'true'
        run: |
          pkg=$(grep '^name:' pubspec.yaml | awk '{print $2}')
          ver="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
          served() { curl -fsSL "https://pub.dev/api/packages/$pkg" 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.latest.version' || true; }
          # The push-run and release-run twins of the same tag both land here
          # (serialized by the job concurrency group): the loser must see the
          # version already served and exit green, not fail on a re-upload.
          if [ "$(served)" = "$ver" ]; then
            echo "::notice::pub.dev already serves $pkg $ver — nothing to publish"
            exit 0
          fi
          dart pub token add https://pub.dev --env-var PUB_TOKEN || true
          (cd /tmp/publish-stage && dart pub publish --force)
          # Verify the upload actually landed (#554, #611): pub.dev CDN
          # propagation takes minutes (v0.1.411: upload accepted 05:00:39Z,
          # latest flipped 05:04Z — the old 5x3s poll sampled at ~16s, saw
          # the stale version, and hard-errored a healthy release). Poll
          # immediately (fast path when propagation is instant), then every
          # 30s for up to 11 min (server-quoted 10 min + margin) before
          # declaring a mismatch; a REAL failure after the full window
          # still fails loudly (#554's guard).
          ok=""
          deadline=$((SECONDS + 660))
          while :; do
            polled=$(served)
            echo "poll: pub.dev serves '$polled' (want $ver, t=${SECONDS}s)"
            if [ "$polled" = "$ver" ]; then ok=1; break; fi
            if [ "$SECONDS" -ge "$deadline" ]; then break; fi
            sleep 30
          done
          if [ -z "$ok" ]; then
            echo "::error::tag $GITHUB_REF_NAME processed but pub.dev still serves '$(served)' after 11 min of polling — publish did not upload. Manual publish needed (see #554)."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "pub.dev verified: $pkg $ver"

  binaries:
    name: Build native binaries
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 45
    # Tag pushes (annotated, via PAT) and `release: published` events both
    # build the matrix. Since v0.1.370 the daily-publish plan creates
    # releases through the API — a lightweight tag with NO push event —
    # which silently starved linux/windows CLI assets (they existed only
    # while tags were still PAT-pushed, up to v0.1.369). The release event
    # fires for every creation path, so the matrix can never be starved
    # again.
    # Same !cancelled() pattern as the release job: the transitive skip
    # through always()-quality-gate starved this matrix on tag pushes and
    # release events alike (fa#456) — no linux/windows CLI assets since
    # v0.1.370. The explicit gate check keeps failed-gate runs from
    # building publishable binaries.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: write # attach assets to the GitHub Release
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - runner: windows-latest
            os: windows
            arch: x64
            archive: zip
          - runner: macos-latest
            os: macos
            arch: arm64
            archive: tar
          # Intel Mac runner (macos-13 is retired; AOT cannot cross-compile
          # macos_x64 from arm64 — only linux_* targets cross).
          - runner: macos-15-intel
            os: macos
            arch: x64
            archive: tar
          - runner: ubuntu-latest
            os: linux
            arch: x64
            archive: tar
          # Native ARM64 runner — dart build cli does not cross-compile.
          - runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            os: linux
            arch: arm64
            archive: tar
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      # gh-1522: the committed pubspec carries the 0.0.0-dev placeholder —
      # the TAG is the version (the retired flow compared tag vs pubspec
      # because a bot commit bumped the file; that commit path is gone).
      # Guard the placeholder here and stamp the bundle version from the tag.
      - name: Verify committed pubspec carries the placeholder
        # Explicit bash: the default shell on Windows runners is pwsh and
        # the POSIX test below dies there with a ParserError.
        shell: bash
        run: |
          placeholder=$(grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml | awk '{print $2}')
          if [ "$placeholder" != "0.0.0-dev" ]; then
            echo "::error::committed pubspec.yaml version is '$placeholder', expected the 0.0.0-dev placeholder (gh-1522) — a hand-bump desyncs the tag-derived builds. Revert pubspec.yaml."
            exit 1
          fi

      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: Build CLI bundle
        shell: bash
        run: |
          # gh-1522: the bundle version rides the TAG (GITHUB_REF_NAME), not
          # the committed placeholder pubspec.
          version="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
          # dart build cli produces: <output>/bundle/{bin/fah, lib/*.dylib}
          # We rename the executable to `fa`, write version.txt, then archive
          # the whole bundle so the installer can extract bin/ + lib/ together.
          if [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ]; then
            dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=build/out
            mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah.exe build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe
          else
            dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=build/out
            mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah build/out/bundle/bin/fa
            chmod +x build/out/bundle/bin/fa
          fi
          echo "$version" > build/out/bundle/version.txt

      - name: Ad-hoc sign CLI binary (macOS)
        if: matrix.os == 'macos'
        shell: bash
        run: codesign --force --sign - build/out/bundle/bin/fa

      # gh-1280 NG2: «compiles» is not «works» — every release arch boots its
      # binary before the asset is archived/uploaded (same smoke as
      # binaries-pr). The usage marker (cli_help.dart "USAGE") discriminates
      # the real CLI help from a binary that merely prints something.
      - name: Smoke — the binary runs (fa --help)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa"
          [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ] && bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe"
          out=$("$bin" --help)
          echo "$out"
          grep -qi "usage" <<<"$out" || { echo "fa --help did not print usage"; exit 1; }

      - name: Archive bundle
        shell: bash
        run: |
          archive_name="fa-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ matrix.arch }}"
          if [ "${{ matrix.archive }}" = "zip" ]; then
            asset="${archive_name}.zip"
            cd build/out && 7z a -tzip "../../$asset" bundle && cd -
          else
            asset="${archive_name}.tar.gz"
            tar -czf "$asset" -C build/out bundle
          fi
          ls -lh "$asset"

      - name: Upload archive to GitHub Release
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          archive_name="fa-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ matrix.arch }}"
          if [ "${{ matrix.archive }}" = "zip" ]; then
            asset="${archive_name}.zip"
          else
            asset="${archive_name}.tar.gz"
          fi
          # gh release upload needs the release to exist; create it lazily
          # (matrix jobs race here, so a duplicate create is tolerated).
          if ! gh release view "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release create "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" \
              --title "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --generate-notes \
              --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" || true
          fi
          gh release upload "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" "$asset" --clobber --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"

  # Rehostable web SPA bundle (issue #1100): every release ships
  # fa-web-spa.zip — the release web build with <base href> rewritten to
  # ./, so it rehosts on any static host (incl. path-prefixed) or sandboxed
  # iframe with zero edits (docs/web-rehosting.md). Same build command AND
  # base-href as the Pages deploy; scripts/package_web_spa.sh patches the
  # tag on a COPY and enforces the absolute-path guard (AC3) before zipping.
  # Lives here, not in pages.yml: release commits (pubspec/CHANGELOG bumps)
  # fall outside pages.yml's path filters, so a Pages-produced bundle could
  # never attach to the actual release commit.
  web-spa:
    name: Build web SPA bundle
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 30
    # Additive asset: a web-build failure (guard trip, SDK flake) must NOT
    # hold the release hostage — CLI provenance (SHA256SUMS) and the vpinned
    # bump still ship. Job-level continue-on-error reports the job (and its
    # check) as SUCCESS — the failed steps stay visible on the run page for
    # the manual check. Downstream needs see success; the provenance fa-*
    # sweep then deterministically finds no zip (success -> signed,
    # failure -> absent — never a half-updated manifest).
    continue-on-error: true
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: write # attach fa-web-spa.zip to the GitHub Release
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Same pinned SDK as build-web / the release path (#281); EXACT patch
      # pin (#1431): a wildcard re-resolves a new engine build on every
      # 3.47.x patch and moves the canvaskit/skwasm rev-hash dir the size
      # gates track. Bump consciously, with any floor reseed in the same PR.
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.7'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Example app pub get
        # gh-1265 AC2: resolve against the committed lockfile; a
        # pubspec/lockfile skew must fail the PR, not float.
        uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # Same placeholders as the Pages job (both files are gitignored).
      - name: Placeholder .env for the example app
        run: touch [REDACTED:Credential File]

      - name: Placeholder firebase_options.dart for the example app
        run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - name: Build web (release, Pages base)
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: flutter build web --release --base-href /app/

      # Same AC3 cut as the Pages deploy (#1096): the vendored WASI
      # interpreter assets are mobile-only (loaded exclusively through
      # WasiSandboxShell under Android/iOS guards; the web sandbox boots
      # env_factory_stub -> MemoryShell -> CDN pyodide/quickjs), so zipping
      # them into fa-web-spa.zip would ship ~47 MB of dead weight.
      - name: Prune mobile-only wasm interpreter assets (#1096 AC3)
        run: rm -rf flutter_app/build/web/assets/assets/wasm

      - name: Package fa-web-spa.zip (relative base + AC3 guard)
