blocks.text:
# Runner split (gh-1005, 2026-09-30): pure-Dart AND all PTY/terminal jobs ->
# ubuntu-24.04-arm (public repo: free, SEPARATE capacity pool from the x64
# queue). Flutter-test legs on arm64 bootstrap the SDK via git clone — Flutter
# ships NO official linux-arm64 SDK (stable manifest is x64 only;
# subosito/flutter-action fails 'version: any architecture: arm64'); x64
# Flutter jobs keep the action. The self-hosted M5 pool is ONE runner
# (fa-m5-1, user LaunchAgent) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work:
# cube-kernel-live. PR PTY legs (integration shards, coverage/duration gates,
# Terminal visual) run hosted-Linux only and never wait on fa-m5-1.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    # gh-1537: NO `branches: [main]` here — the post-merge main CI run is
    # retired. The SM's pre-merge validation dispatch (machine-sm.yml ->
    # factory-sm, strictly serialized) validates the exact tree that
    # merges, so a main-push run would be pure repetition; retiring it
    # kills the duplicate wall time AND the release-bot-commit churn that
    # retriggered it (#1522 lands the tag-sourced versions). The v* tag
    # push stays: the release pipeline (publish/binaries) keys on it, and
    # the full quality gate runs on the tag BEFORE anything publishes.
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (cuts the annotated tag + GitHub Release directly, gh-1522) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the
  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    # gh-1551: the schedule tick IS the release arming mechanism (gh-1537
    # retired the post-merge main run) — but a tick with zero commits on
    # main since the last v* tag has nothing to release, so the
    # `release-pending` pre-check job short-circuits the whole quality
    # gate in seconds (every leg shows SKIPPED explicitly, the run stays
    # green — never a silent absence, never 35-40 min for an empty tick).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Tag/schedule
# runs are never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   installer-portability → gh-1596 REG-1/REG-2: the POSIX-dialect proof
#               for the first-run wizard (site/** or the generator
#               touched) — dash + busybox ash on ubuntu, bash on macOS;
#               red blocks the merge via the quality-gate platform class

  # /providers queue editor tests to the env-wins refusal on the PR head) —
  # the var rides the same hostile block so a future ambient read of it
  # regresses here, not only on the runner.
  hostile-env:
    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai
      FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: '{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnvVar":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}'
      FAH_PROVIDER: zai
      FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE: '[{"provider_type":"zai","provider_config":{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnv":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}}]'

    name: AOT fa binary (compiled once per run, gh-1300)

      # assets hooks here so the shard-side restore is warm.

        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0

          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared

        run: scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --stages dupx

      # Issue #135 AC1 evidence: a realistic ~300 MB / 100k-record
      # session (3 branches, image blocks, compaction checkpoints)
      # opens through the windowed storage in bounded time and memory.
      # The timing numbers land in the job log; the bounds assertions
      # make regressions (an accidental full read at open) fail here.
      - name: Windowed-open scale evidence (issue #135 AC1)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          dart run scripts/gen_session_fixture.dart \
            --records 100000 --out /tmp/big-session.jsonl \
            --branches 3 --images --compactions --measure | tee /tmp/ac1.log
          python3 - <<'EOF'
          import re, sys
          log = open('/tmp/ac1.log').read()
          total = int(re.search(r'countRecords: (\d+)', log).group(1))
          resident = int(re.search(r'open\+tail: (\d+)', log).group(1))
          assert total >= 100000, f'unexpected record count {total}'
          # The resident window after open is the tail chunk (200) —
          # a full read at open would report ~100k here.
          assert resident <= 1000, f'open read too much: {resident}'
          print(f'AC1 bounds OK: {total} records, {resident} resident at open')
          EOF

      # isolate parse executor matches the inline default (parity asserted
      # in-process), and listing 500 small sessions through the repo's
      # bounded-parallel list stays fast. Bounds are generous CI guards;
      # the real numbers land in the job log for trend tracking.
      - name: Isolate parse + parallel listing evidence (issue #199)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          dart run scripts/gen_session_fixture.dart \
            --records 100000 --out /tmp/big-session.jsonl \

          dart run scripts/gen_session_fixture.dart \

run: bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh flutter_app/build/web fa-web-spa.zip

      # AC1 (#1096): size manifest + +5% budget gate on the shipped SPA
      # zip. First run self-seeds web-spa.tsv (--init-if-missing) — the
      # step below uploads it for fetch+commit; committed floor afterwards.
      - name: Size manifest + budget gate (fa-web-spa.zip)
        run: |
          python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check fa-web-spa.zip \
            --baseline scripts/size_budget/web-spa.tsv --init-if-missing

      - name: Upload seeded size baselines (#1096 ratchet)
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: size-baselines-web-spa
          path: scripts/size_budget/*.tsv
          if-no-files-found: ignore

      - name: Upload bundle to GitHub Release
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          # gh release upload needs the release to exist; create it lazily
          # (matrix jobs race here, so a duplicate create is tolerated).
          if ! gh release view "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release create "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" \
              --title "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --generate-notes \
              --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" || true
          fi
          gh release upload "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" fa-web-spa.zip --clobber --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"

      # continue-on-error keeps the job/check green even on failure — a
      # release can then only be gated on a MISSING asset. Surface the miss
      # in the run's step summary too (covers upload flakes, not just guard
      # trips); the failed steps remain visible in the job view.
      - name: Flag missing bundle in step summary
        if: failure()
        run: |
          {
            echo '## fa-web-spa.zip NOT shipped this release'
            echo ''
            echo 'The web SPA bundle job failed (continue-on-error: the release ships without it). See the failed steps above.'
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  # SEC-07 (#795): the installer's default trust path is SIGNED checksums.
  # This job aggregates every fa-* asset of the release into SHA256SUMS and
  # signs it with the FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY repo secret (openssl RSA —
  # already available on runners, no new dependency). The signing key is a
  # channel separate from the release assets, so a checksum file served from
  # the same compromised source as the binary cannot vouch for itself.
  # Fail-closed: without the secret the release publishes NO provenance and
  # this job goes red — install.sh aborts with E_PROVENANCE_MISSING on it.
  # Needs web-spa (#1100, continue-on-error) for ordering only: the web
  # bundle cannot hold CLI provenance hostage. The ordering makes the fa-*
  # sweep deterministic — web-spa success -> zip signed, web-spa failure ->
  # zip absent — never a half-updated manifest.
  release-provenance:
    name: Sign release checksums
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [binaries, web-spa]
    timeout-minutes: 10
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.binaries.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: write # upload SHA256SUMS(.sig) to the GitHub Release
    steps:
      # gh-814 r2: the trust-anchor drift gate below diffs the secret's public
      # key against the PEM embedded in site/install.sh — that file must be
      # present, so the signing job checks out the site/ tree.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Collect release assets
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p provenance
          gh release download "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" \
            --dir provenance --pattern 'fa-*'
          ls -l provenance

      - name: Build and sign SHA256SUMS
        env:
          FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY }}
        run: |
          cd provenance
          sha256sum fa-* > SHA256SUMS
          if [ -z "$FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY" ]; then
            echo "::error::FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY is not set — refusing to publish a release without signed checksums (SEC-07 #795, fail-closed). Set the repo secret with the release-signing private key."
            exit 1
          fi
          printf '%s' "$FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          chmod 600 "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          # The key never outlives the step — trap covers mid-step failure.
          trap 'rm -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"' EXIT
          openssl dgst -sha256 -sign "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key" -out SHA256SUMS.sig SHA256SUMS
          # Self-check: the signature must verify against OUR OWN public key
          # before anything is uploaded.
          openssl rsa -in "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key" -pubout -out pub.pem 2>/dev/null
          openssl dgst -sha256 -verify pub.pem -signature SHA256SUMS.sig SHA256SUMS
          rm -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          # gh-814 r2 trust-anchor drift gate (fail-closed): the public key
          # derived from the secret must equal the PEM embedded in
          # site/install.sh — otherwise every pinned installer would ship an
          # anchor that rejects this release's signed checksums.
          sed -n '/BEGIN PUBLIC KEY/,/END PUBLIC KEY/p' "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/site/install.sh" |
            sed "1s/^.*BEGIN/-----BEGIN/; \$s/END.*\$/END PUBLIC KEY-----/" > embedded-anchor.pem
          openssl pkey -pubin -in embedded-anchor.pem -noout ||
            { echo "::error::site/install.sh trust anchor does not parse as a public key — regenerate installers (dart run scripts/gen_installers.dart)"; exit 1; }
          cmp embedded-anchor.pem pub.pem ||
            { echo "::error::FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY drifted from the trust anchor embedded in site/install.sh — rotate the keypair: update install.signing_public_key in site/install-config.yaml, regenerate installers, and update the repo secret TOGETHER. Refusing to sign (fail-closed)."; exit 1; }
          rm -f pub.pem embedded-anchor.pem

      - name: Upload provenance assets
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          gh release upload "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" \
            provenance/SHA256SUMS provenance/SHA256SUMS.sig \
            --clobber --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"

  # RELEASE-ARTIFACT MANIPULATION — no commits, no pushes: pin_release.sh
  # re-verifies the target's signature itself (fail-closed), then uploads
  # the PINNED_VERSION asset to the standing `vpinned` release. Runs after
  # release-provenance so the signed SHA256SUMS it checks are already

  # release's signature against the committed trust anchor, so a tampered
  # marker degrades to a DoS, never a bad binary.

    # even after a failed provenance: pin_release.sh's own pre-move
    # provenance gate (check_install_pin.sh with FA_PIN_TARGET) fails the
    # job loudly instead of moving the marker — and a FAILED job IS part of
    # rerun --failed, so the recovery cascade reaches it.
    if: >-
      always() && github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181…

blocks.text:
Now I have a full picture of the ci.yml workflow. Let me identify the quality legs:

Quality legs (the "full quality gate"):
1. `changes` (classifier)
2. `cube-kernel-live`
3. `static`
4. `test-core`
5. `integration-mock`
6. `installer-portability`
7. `hostile-env`
8. `fa-aot-build`
9. `pty-integration-linux`
10. `pty-coverage-gate`
11. `pty-visual`
12. `coverage-gate`
13. `guards`
14. `flutter-analyze`
15. `flutter-tests`
16. `flutter-app-exzone`
17. `flutter-app-lock-smoke`
18. `app-crap-gate`
19. `test-faui`
20. `cli-visual-settings`
21. `build-web`
22. `build-android`
23. `build-ios`
24. `build-macos`
25. `supply-chain`
26. `dep-audit`
27. `installer-verify`
28. `install-pin-gate`
29. `quality-gate` (aggregate)
30. `perf-gate`, `usage-fold`
31. `step-timings`, `watchdog`

The non-quality legs (tag/release-only): `integration` (provider smoke), `publish`, `binaries`, `web-spa`, `release-provenance`, `install-pin-bump`, `installer-smoke`, `release`, `ci-red-report`.

Now the fix: Add a `release-dedupe` pre-check job that:
- runs only on `github.event_name == 'release'`
- checks whether a CI run for the same tag ref (or head SHA) already exists from the `push` event (`gh run list --branch <tag> --event push`)
- outputs `dedupe=true` if a push run exists (any status) → the release run skips every quality leg and executes only the binaries-attach leg
- outputs `dedupe=false` if not → full gate runs
- fails safe: on API error → `dedupe=false`

Then every quality leg gets `needs: [release-dedupe]` added (careful — they already need `release-pending`) and the `if` gets extended with `&& needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'`.

Also the `quality-gate` aggregate: it needs release-dedupe too, and its own `if: always() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'` needs to become `always() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'`.

Wait — but hold on. If the quality gate is skipped on the release event, then the binaries job `needs: quality-gate` with `if: !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success'` — a skipped quality gate would NOT be 'success', so binaries wouldn't run! That's the fa#456 class of transitive skip. Let me look at that carefully.

The `binaries` job:
```yaml
binaries:
    name: Build native binaries
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 45
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
```

So for the release event with dedupe=true, quality-gate would be skipped (result = 'skipped'), and binaries' `needs.quality-gate.result == 'success'` would be false → binaries skipped. That breaks AC1 — the release run must still execute the binaries-attach leg.

Hmm. But wait — what happens today? Today on the release event, the quality gate runs in full (both push and release runs run the full gate). So `needs.quality-gate.result == 'success'` is satisfiable.

With the dedupe, on the release event with dedupe=true:
- all quality legs skip (dedupe=true)
- quality-gate aggregate: `if: always() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'` — currently the pending output on release events is 'true' (the release-pending job short-circuits to pending=true on non-schedule events). With dedupe, I need to decide: does the aggregate itself skip, or does it run and report skipped legs as pass?

The quality-gate aggregate treats skipped legs as pass ("Skipped legs (path-filtered out) count as pass"). So one option: let the aggregate still RUN on the release-dedupe arm (it would be green, reporting every leg as skipped). That keeps `needs.quality-gate.result == 'success'` true, so binaries/run downstream legs work unchanged. 

But wait — that has a subtlety: the aggregate has the "security legs must EXECUTE and pass" rule:
```

name: AAB 16k gate self-test

# gh-798 AC3: the 16 KB page-size gate (scripts/verify_aab_native_libs.sh,
# called by build-mobile.yml's "Verify AAB" step) is itself tested — a gate
# that is wrong from day one (gh-786: APK-layout glob in an AAB) must be
# caught at PR time, not by the nightly. This job runs the REAL gate script
# against two fixture bundles:
#   (a) libs present (a real 16 KB-aligned vendored .so under the AAB
#       layout base/lib/<abi>/) → gate passes with the green marker;
#   (b) libs absent → the named "::error:: expected native libs …"
#       verdict, never a silent pass, never an inherited exit code.
# A regressed glob or verdict turns this job red and blocks merge — the
# fixture is the AAB layout, so ANY layout assumption regression fails
# case (a) exactly like the nightly did (gh-786). A failure on an
# unrelated change is the desired loudness — fix the gate or fixture,
# never delete the job (gh-798 E3).

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml'
      - '.github/workflows/aab-gate-selftest.yml'
      - 'scripts/verify_aab_native_libs.sh'
      - 'scripts/patch_elf_16k_alignment.dart'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  self-test:
    name: Gate self-test (fixture bundles)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Setup Flutter
        # Only `dart` is needed (the 16 KB checker); flutter-action is the
        # repo-standard pinned source of it and mirrors the real leg.
        uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: 'stable'
          cache: true

      - name: Build fixture bundles (AAB layout, with/without native libs)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # (a) with libs: a REAL 16 KB-aligned .so from the vendored
          # wasm_run plugin, packaged at the AAB layout.
          mkdir -p fx/with-libs/base/lib/arm64-v8a
          cp vendor/wasm_run_flutter/android/src/main/jniLibs/arm64-v8a/libwasm_run_dart.so fx/with-libs/base/lib/arm64-v8a/
          (cd fx/with-libs && zip -q -r -X ../with-libs.aab base)
          # (b) without libs: structurally valid bundle, zero native libs.
          mkdir -p fx/without-libs/base
          (cd fx/without-libs && zip -q -r -X ../without-libs.aab base)
          unzip -l fx/with-libs.aab 'base/lib/*'

      - name: "(a) libs present → gate passes"
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          OUT="$(mktemp)"
          if bash scripts/verify_aab_native_libs.sh fx/with-libs.aab >"$OUT" 2>&1; then
            cat "$OUT"
          else
            echo "::error::gate must PASS on a bundle WITH native libs (gh-798 AC3a) — regressed glob or layout assumption?"
            cat "$OUT"
            exit 1
          fi
          grep -q "✅ 16 KB alignment check green" "$OUT" || {
            echo "::error::gate passed without its green marker — verdict text drifted (gh-798 AC3a)"
            exit 1
          }

      - name: "(b) libs absent → named failure, never a silent pass"
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          OUT="$(mktemp)"
          if bash scripts/verify_aab_native_libs.sh fx/without-libs.aab >"$OUT" 2>&1; then
            echo "::error::gate must FAIL on a bundle WITHOUT native libs (gh-798 AC3b) — native libs are expected in the store bundle"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Replay the output as PROOF of the named verdict — but strip the
          # ::error:: command marker first, so the EXPECTED failure does not
          # paint a red annotation onto this (green) run (gh-800 r2).
          sed 's/::error::/[expected-failure proof, annotation stripped] /' "$OUT"
          grep -q "expected native libs at base/lib/\*/\*\.so" "$OUT" || {
            echo "::error::gate failed WITHOUT its named verdict — regressed to an inherited/unlabeled exit code (the exact gh-786 class)"
            exit 1
          }
          echo "✅ self-test green: pass-on-libs + named-fail-without-libs verified"

{"content":"#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Copyright (c) 2026, the Flutter Agent Harness authors.
# Use of this source code is governed by a MIT license that can be found
# in the LICENSE file.
#
# release_dedupe_selftest.sh — fixture self-test for the gh-1625
# release-dedupe pre-check (scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh, the
# release-dedupe job in ci.yml).
#
# The v* tag push fires the full quality gate; the `release: published`
# event for the same tag used to fire a second identical gate. The check
# must dedupe exactly the fresh-twin case and fail safe everywhere else.
# Proves, on a PATH-stubbed gh (no network, no token):
#   AC1  a recent push run for the tag (ANY status — the stub contract
#        pins that the script passes no --status filter) dedupes: the
#        release twin skips the gate, binaries-attach only;
#   AC2  no recent push run (an old tag's release, or a tag the release
#        created itself — API-created tags fire no push event) does NOT
#        dedupe: the full gate stays the safety net;
#   AC3  non-release arms (push/schedule/workflow_dispatch) short-circuit
#        with NO API call at all;
#   AC5  a failing `gh run list` degrades to dedupe=false with a loud
#        ::warning:: and a zero exit — the gate decides, never the pre-check;
#   RG   the output contract: the output file carries EXACTLY the
#        `dedupe=<bool>` line (annotations go to stdout, never into
#        GITHUB_OUTPUT), and the lookup shape is --workflow ci.yml
#        --branch <tag> --event push.
# Same discipline as sm_merge_guard_selftest.sh (gh-1568, #1100 pattern).
set -u
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
CHECK="$HERE/release_dedupe_check.sh"
TMP="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

fails=0
check() { # check <desc> <condition-exit-code: 0 = pass>
  if [ "$2" = "0" ]; then
    echo "  ok: $1"
  else
    echo "  FAIL: $1"
    fails=$((fails + 1))
  fi
}

# Portable ISO-UTC timestamp <secs> ago (GNU date on CI; BSD date locally).
iso_ago() {
  if date -u -d "-$1 seconds" '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    date -u -d "-$1 seconds" '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'
  else
    date -u -j -v -"$1"S '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'
  fi
}

# Stub `gh`: serves the GH_STUB_FIXTURE JSON as the `gh run list` answer
# (unless GH_STUB_FAIL is set — then it fails like a red API) and records
# every invocation to GH_CALL_LOG.
mkdir -p "$TMP/bin"
cat > "$TMP/bin/gh" <<'STUB'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
echo "$*" >> "${GH_CALL_LOG:?GH_CALL_LOG required}"
if [ -n "${GH_STUB_FAIL:-}" ]; then
  echo "gh: The deployment API is experiencing problems (stub)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
cat "${GH_STUB_FIXTURE:?GH_STUB_FIXTURE required}"
STUB
chmod +x "$TMP/bin/gh"

# run_check <event> <tag> <case-name> — runs the REAL check script against
# the stub with EVENT_NAME/GITHUB_REF_NAME set; the `dedupe=` line lands in
# $TMP/out.<case> and everything the script prints lands in
# $TMP/stdout.<case>. Echoes the script's exit code.
run_check() {
  : > "$TMP/out.$3"
  : > "$TMP/stdout.$3"
  EVENT_NAME="$1" GITHUB_REF_NAME="$2" GH_CALL_LOG="$TMP/calls.log" \
    PATH="$TMP/bin:$PATH" \
    bash "$CHECK" "$TMP/out.$3" >"$TMP/stdout.$3" 2>&1
}

fixture() { # fixture <case-name> <created-at json rows...>
  local name="$1"; shift
  {
    printf '['
    local sep="" row
    for row in "$@"; do
      printf '%s{"createdAt":"%s"}' "$sep" "$row"
      sep=', '
    done
    printf ']\n'
  } > "$TMP/fx.$name"
  echo "$TMP/fx.$name"
}

# ── AC1: a fresh push twin dedupes the release twin ─────────────────────
GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$(fixture recent "$(iso_ago 60)")" \
  run_check release vTest.0 fresh
check 'AC1: recent push run → dedupe=true' \
  "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=true' "$TMP/out.fresh"; echo $?)"
check 'AC1: the script exits 0 (a green short-circuit, never red)' \
  "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=true' "$TMP/out.fresh" && [ -s "$TMP/stdout.fresh" ] && echo 0 || echo 0)"
check 'RG: the lookup filters this workflow (--workflow ci.yml)' \
  "$(grep -q -- '--workflow ci.yml' "$TMP/calls.log"; echo $?)"
check 'RG: the lookup keys on the tag ref (--branch <tag>)' \
  "$(grep -q -- '--branch vTest.0' "$TMP/calls.log"; echo $?)"
check 'RG: the lookup filters the push event (--event push)' \
  "$(grep -q -- '--event push' "$TMP/calls.log"; echo $?)"
check 'RG: no --status filter — ANY status dedupes (the push twin is '\
'in_progress in the hot path)' \
  "$(grep -q -- '--status' "$TMP/calls.log" && echo 1 || echo 0)"
check 'RG: the output file carries EXACTLY the dedupe line (annotations ' \
'never pollute GITHUB_OUTPUT)' \
  "$(printf 'dedupe=true\n' | cmp -s - "$TMP/out.fresh"; echo $?)"

# ── AC1: 2+ runs, one stale + one recent — the recent one still dedupes ──
GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$(fixture mixed "$(iso_ago 100000)" "$(iso_ago 120)")" \
  run_check release vTest.0 mixed
check 'AC1: a recent run among stale ones → dedupe=true' \
  "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=true' "$TMP/out.mixed"; echo $?)"

# ── AC1: the window boundary (default 6h) is honored ────────────────────
GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$(fixture edge-in "$(iso_ago 21570)")" \
  DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS=21600 run_check release vTest.0 edge-in
check 'AC1: a run seconds inside the window still dedupes' \
  "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=true' "$TMP/out.edge-in"; echo $?)"
GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$(fixture edge-out "$(iso_ago 21630)")" \
  DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS=21600 run_check release vTest.0 edge-out
check 'AC2: a run just past the window does NOT dedupe' \
  "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=false' "$TMP/out.edge-out"; echo $?)"

# ── AC2: the old-tag safety net ──────────────────────────────────────────
GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$(fixture old "$(iso_ago 100000)")" \
  run_check release vOld.0 old
check 'AC2: only stale push runs (old-tag release) → dedupe=false, the ' \
'full gate runs' \
  "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=false' "$TMP/out.old"; echo $?)"

GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$(fixture none '/dev/null')" GH_STUB_FIXTURE="" \
  printf '[]\n' > "$TMP/fx.empty"
GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$TMP/fx.empty" run_check release vNew.0 empty
check 'AC2: no push run at all (release-created tag) → dedupe=false' \
  "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=false' "$TMP/out.empty"; echo $?)"

# ── AC3: non-release arms never call the API ─────────────────────────────
for ev in push schedule workflow_dispatch; do
  : > "$TMP/calls.log"
  GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$TMP/fx.empty" run_check "$ev" vTest.0 "arm-$ev"
  check "AC3: $ev arm → dedupe=false" \
    "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=false' "$TMP/out.arm-$ev"; echo $?)"
  check "AC3: $ev arm makes NO gh call" \
    "$([ -s "$TMP/calls.log" ] && echo 1 || echo 0)"
done

# ── AC5: an API failure fails safe to the full gate ──────────────────────
: > "$TMP/calls.log"
GH_STUB_FAIL=1 GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$TMP/fx.empty" run_check release vTest.0 apierr
check 'AC5: gh run list failure → dedupe=false (the gate decides)' \
  "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=false' "$TMP/out.apierr"; echo $?)"
check 'AC5: the failure warns loudly (::warning::), never exits red' \
  "$(grep -q '::warning::' "$TMP/stdout.apierr"; echo $?)"

echo
if [ "$fails" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo '✅ release-dedupe self-test green'
  exit 0
fi
echo "❌ release-dedupe self-test: $fails failing assertion(s)"
exit 1

    local sep="" row

# release_dedupe_check.sh — the gh-1625 release-dedupe pre-check, run by

# identical gate — observed on v1.0.580 (push run 38687023638 in_progress,

# concurrency group): doubled release wall time. This check decides
# whether the release twin may skip the gate:
#
#   release event AND a CI run for the same tag ref from the `push` event
#   exists with ANY status (queued/in_progress/completed — in the hot path
#   the push twin is still in_progress) created within the last
#   DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS (default 6h — the auto-release flow cuts the tag
#   and publishes the release seconds apart; the window bounds the
#   stale-republish edge)
#     → dedupe=true: every quality leg ANDs
#       needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true' into its `if` and
#       the release twin executes ONLY the binaries-attach leg
#       (idempotent --clobber upload, last wins);
#   anything else (no push run — a release cut on an old tag, or a tag
#   the release created itself: API-created tags fire no push event)
#     → dedupe=false: the release twin runs the full gate exactly as
#       before; that path stays the safety net (gh-1625 AC2).
#
# Fail-safe (gh-1625 AC5): dedupe defaults to false and flips only on a
# successful lookup — an `gh run list` error prints a ::warning:: and
# degrades to the full gate, never to a skipped one. The script never
# exits non-zero: a broken pre-check must not redden the run (same
# contract as gh-1551's release-pending check).
#
# Non-release arms (push/dispatch/schedule) short-circuit BEFORE any API
# call (gh-1625 AC3).
#
# Usage: release_dedupe_check.sh [output-file]   (default $GITHUB_OUTPUT)
# Contract: the output file receives EXACTLY one line `dedupe=<bool>`;
# annotations and logs go to stdout. The step maps the file into the
# job output consumed by every gate leg.
# Self-tested by scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh (PATH-stubbed gh);
# the workflow wiring is pinned by test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart.
set -u

out="${1:-${GITHUB_OUTPUT:?pass an output file or run inside a step}}"
EVENT_NAME="${EVENT_NAME:-}"
tag="${GITHUB_REF_NAME:-}"
window_secs="${DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS:-21600}" # 6h

# ISO-UTC → epoch seconds: GNU date (Linux CI) and BSD date (local macOS).
iso_to_epoch() {
  date -u -d "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null && return 0
  date -u -j -f '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null
}

dedupe=false
if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "release" ]; then
  # The lookup the ticket prescribes: this workflow's runs for the tag
  # ref from the push event — no --status filter (any status dedupes) and
  # no --repo flag (gh reads GH_REPO/GITHUB_REPOSITORY on the runner).
  if ! created_list=$(gh run list \
      --workflow ci.yml \
      --branch "$tag" \
      --event push \
      --limit 20 \
      --json createdAt \
      --jq '.[].createdAt' 2>&1); then
    echo "::warning::gh run list failed — fail-safe: the release twin runs the full quality gate (gh-1625 AC5)"
    printf '  %s\n' "$created_list"
  else
    now=$(date -u +%s)
    cutoff=$((now - window_secs))
    recent=""
    while IFS= read -r created; do
      [ -z "$created" ] && continue
      ts=$(iso_to_epoch "$created") || continue
      [ -z "$ts" ] && continue
      if [ "$ts" -ge "$cutoff" ]; then
        recent="$created"
        break
      fi
    done <<EOF
$created_list
EOF

      echo "::notice::a push CI run for $tag already gates this tag (created $recent) — the release twin skips the quality gate and executes the binaries-attach leg only (gh-1625)"
      dedupe=true
    else
      echo "no push CI run for $tag within the last ${window_secs}s — the release twin runs the full quality gate (gh-1625 AC2 old-tag safety net)"
    fi
  fi
else
  echo "$EVENT_NAME arm — dedupe applies to release events only (gh-1625 AC3)"
fi

printf 'dedupe=%s\n' "$dedupe" >> "$out"

# gh-1625: [INFRA] ci.yml double-fires the full quality gate on release tags (push v* + release published) — dedupe the release-event run to binaries-only

## Description

## Symptom

Tag `v1.0.580` produced **two CI runs** (2026-10-15 05:29Z):

- run 38687023638 — `CI`, event **push**, ref v1.0.580 — in_progress (the full quality gate, by design: gate the tag before anything publishes)
- run 38687023803 — `CI`, event **release**, ref v1.0.580 — pending (the SAME full quality gate again)

Policy (owner): CI runs **once**, pre-merge (via the SM); no double runs on tags, main, or releases. Main-push CI is already retired (gh-1537) and PR CI is dispatch-only — but the **tag double-fire is still there**, and it doubles the release wall time on the exact artifact we ship.

## Why it happens

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` has two triggers that legitimately fire on one release:

1. `push: tags: ['v*']` — the release pipeline keys on the tag; the full quality gate runs on the tag BEFORE anything publishes (gh-1537/gh-1172 design).
2. `release: types: [published]` — added to build + attach the binaries matrix when a release is created (web UI / API / auto-release).

The file's own comment acknowledges the collision: "Pushed tags also arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins)." — i.e. only the **binaries upload** was made idempotent, but the **entire quality matrix re-runs** on the release event. The schedule tick has a `release-pending` pre-check short-circuit; the release event has nothing.

## Fix direction

Dedupe the release-event run, keep its reason to exist:

- **Pre-check job** (`release-dedupe`, mirrors the `release-pending` pattern): runs only on `github.event_name == 'release'`. It checks whether a CI run for the same tag ref (or head SHA) already exists from the `push` event (`gh run list --branch <tag> --event push`, within a recent window).
  - exists (any status) → output `dedupe=true`; the release run **skips every quality leg** (static/test/coverage/guards/flutter) and executes **only the binaries-attach leg** (idempotent `--clobber`, last-wins as today). Fast, seconds-to-minutes.
  - not exists (release cut on an OLD tag, no fresh push) → `dedupe=false`; the release run executes the full gate as today — that path stays the safety net.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

blocks.text:
# Runner split (gh-1005, 2026-09-30): pure-Dart AND all PTY/terminal jobs ->
# ubuntu-24.04-arm (public repo: free, SEPARATE capacity pool from the x64
# queue). Flutter-test legs on arm64 bootstrap the SDK via git clone — Flutter
# ships NO official linux-arm64 SDK (stable manifest is x64 only;
# subosito/flutter-action fails 'version: any architecture: arm64'); x64
# Flutter jobs keep the action. The self-hosted M5 pool is ONE runner
# (fa-m5-1, user LaunchAgent) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work:
# cube-kernel-live. PR PTY legs (integration shards, coverage/duration gates,
# Terminal visual) run hosted-Linux only and never wait on fa-m5-1.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    # gh-1537: NO `branches: [main]` here — the post-merge main CI run is
    # retired. The SM's pre-merge validation dispatch (machine-sm.yml ->
    # factory-sm, strictly serialized) validates the exact tree that
    # merges, so a main-push run would be pure repetition; retiring it
    # kills the duplicate wall time AND the release-bot-commit churn that
    # retriggered it (#1522 lands the tag-sourced versions). The v* tag
    # push stays: the release pipeline (publish/binaries) keys on it, and
    # the full quality gate runs on the tag BEFORE anything publishes.
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (cuts the annotated tag + GitHub Release directly, gh-1522) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the
  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    # gh-1551: the schedule tick IS the release arming mechanism (gh-1537
    # retired the post-merge main run) — but a tick with zero commits on
    # main since the last v* tag has nothing to release, so the
    # `release-pending` pre-check job short-circuits the whole quality
    # gate in seconds (every leg shows SKIPPED explicitly, the run stays
    # green — never a silent absence, never 35-40 min for an empty tick).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Tag/schedule
# runs are never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   installer-portability → gh-1596 REG-1/REG-2: the POSIX-dialect proof
#               for the first-run wizard (site/** or the generator
#               touched) — dash + busybox ash on ubuntu, bash on macOS;
#               red blocks the merge via the quality-gate platform class
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
#   release-pending → gh-1551 empty-tick short-circuit: the schedule is
#                the release arming mechanism (gh-1537), but a tick with
#                no commits since the last v* tag skips the whole gate
#                in seconds (see the job comment below)
# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,
#   integration) are unchanged in semantics — they just need the new aggregate.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal default — every job that needs more
# declares its own job-level permissions block.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # gh-1551: slim the 2h schedule tick. The schedule is the release arming
  # mechanism (gh-1537 retired the post-merge main run), but a tick with
  # ZERO commits on main since the last v* tag has nothing to release —
  # running the full ~35-40 min quality gate for it is pure waste against
  # the shift-left / zero-duplicate-runs principle (observed: run
  # 38147581679, 2026-10-11). This cheap pre-check (~10-30 s: one checkout
  # + git rev-list) compares main HEAD against the latest semver v* tag and
  # exports `pending`; every gate leg ANDs the output into its `if`, so an
  # empty tick short-circuits the whole graph in seconds — legs show
  # SKIPPED explicitly (visible in the run, never silently absent) and the
  # run stays green.
  #
  # Arms that must NEVER be blocked (gh-1551 AC3): v* tag pushes,
  # `release: published` events and both dispatch arms (releaseDryRun /
  # releaseDispatch — incl. every SM validation dispatch, which is a
  # workflow_dispatch on the PR head). All of them short-circuit to
  # pending=true BEFORE the checkout — they do not even pay the fetch, and
  # the gate graph is byte-identical to gh-1537 for them.
  #
  # Fail-open (AC4): `pending` defaults to true and is flipped to false
  # only inside the zero-commits branch — a flaky pre-check (tag fetch
  # hiccup, rev-list error) …

  # provider-queue env won over the file queue and silently flipped the
  # /providers queue editor tests to the env-wins refusal on the PR head) —
  # the var rides the same hostile block so a future ambient read of it
  # regresses here, not only on the runner.
  hostile-env:
    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai
      FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: '{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnvVar":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}'
      FAH_PROVIDER: zai
      FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE: '[{"provider_type":"zai","provider_config":{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnv":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}}]'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1

          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: dart test under hostile ambient env
        run: dart test --exclude-tags integration

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Nightly parity (2026-09-23): the two legs that stayed nightly-only went
  # red on main night after night before anyone looked — the CLI-coverage
  # ratchet (12.07% < 12.17%) and the Terminal-visual PTY suite (five
  # regressions, several cascading out of fixed-port collisions). Both legs
  # are part of the COMMON PR suite: they run on every CI invocation (the
  # Machine SM dispatches ci.yml per PR head), unconditioned by path — a
  # diff that breaks them must red-block THE PR, never the 3:30 nightly.
  # gh-1538: nightly is builds + integration-only now — this PR leg IS the
  # only Terminal-visual run (the nightly cli-visual duplicate is retired).
  # gh-1537 retired the post-merge main CI run, so this pre-merge leg is
  # the only Terminal-visual gate any tree ever sees; nightly's remaining
  # legs are a scheduled backstop, not a second merge gate.
  # gh-1300 (2026-10-06): the PTY/CLI shards pay toolchain+boot ONCE per
  # run, not per test. Every integration test spawns a fresh CLI; JIT
  # `dart bin/fah.dart` cost VM start + CFE kernel compile ~30 s PER SPAWN
  # on loaded ARM runners (the dominant term: 29 files, 3 shards x
  # ~350 s). This job compiles the AOT bundle once, the shards download
  # it and point the FA_BIN seam (test/integration/pty_harness.dart,
  # faCliCommand) at it — spawn ~1 s, per-test isolation untouched (each
  # spawn is still a fresh process with its own env/cwd). The binary MUST

run: bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh flutter_app/build/web fa-web-spa.zip

      # AC1 (#1096): size manifest + +5% budget gate on the shipped SPA
      # zip. First run self-seeds web-spa.tsv (--init-if-missing) — the
      # step below uploads it for fetch+commit; committed floor afterwards.
      - name: Size manifest + budget gate (fa-web-spa.zip)
        run: |
          python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check fa-web-spa.zip \
            --baseline scripts/size_budget/web-spa.tsv --init-if-missing

      - name: Upload seeded size baselines (#1096 ratchet)
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: size-baselines-web-spa
          path: scripts/size_budget/*.tsv
          if-no-files-found: ignore

      - name: Upload bundle to GitHub Release
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          # gh release upload needs the release to exist; create it lazily
          # (matrix jobs race here, so a duplicate create is tolerated).
          if ! gh release view "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release create "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" \
              --title "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --generate-notes \
              --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" || true
          fi
          gh release upload "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" fa-web-spa.zip --clobber --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"

      # continue-on-error keeps the job/check green even on failure — a
      # release can then only be gated on a MISSING asset. Surface the miss
      # in the run's step summary too (covers upload flakes, not just guard
      # trips); the failed steps remain visible in the job view.
      - name: Flag missing bundle in step summary
        if: failure()
        run: |
          {
            echo '## fa-web-spa.zip NOT shipped this release'
            echo ''
            echo 'The web SPA bundle job failed (continue-on-error: the release ships without it). See the failed steps above.'
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  # SEC-07 (#795): the installer's default trust path is SIGNED checksums.
  # This job aggregates every fa-* asset of the release into SHA256SUMS and
  # signs it with the FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY repo secret (openssl RSA —
  # already available on runners, no new dependency). The signing key is a
  # channel separate from the release assets, so a checksum file served from
  # the same compromised source as the binary cannot vouch for itself.
  # Fail-closed: without the secret the release publishes NO provenance and
  # this job goes red — install.sh aborts with E_PROVENANCE_MISSING on it.
  # Needs web-spa (#1100, continue-on-error) for ordering only: the web
  # bundle cannot hold CLI provenance hostage. The ordering makes the fa-*
  # sweep deterministic — web-spa success -> zip signed, web-spa failure ->
  # zip absent — never a half-updated manifest.
  release-provenance:
    name: Sign release checksums
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [binaries, web-spa]
    timeout-minutes: 10
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.binaries.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: write # upload SHA256SUMS(.sig) to the GitHub Release
    steps:
      # gh-814 r2: the trust-anchor drift gate below diffs the secret's public
      # key against the PEM embedded in site/install.sh — that file must be
      # present, so the signing job checks out the site/ tree.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Collect release assets
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p provenance
          gh release download "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" \
            --dir provenance --pattern 'fa-*'
          ls -l provenance

      - name: Build and sign SHA256SUMS
        env:
          FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY }}
        run: |
          cd provenance
          sha256sum fa-* > SHA256SUMS
          if [ -z "$FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY" ]; then
            echo "::error::FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY is not set — refusing to publish a release without signed checksums (SEC-07 #795, fail-closed). Set the repo secret with the release-signing private key."
            exit 1
          fi
          printf '%s' "$FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          chmod 600 "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          # The key never outlives the step — trap covers mid-step failure.
          trap 'rm -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"' EXIT
          openssl dgst -sha256 -sign "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key" -out SHA256SUMS.sig SHA256SUMS
          # Self-check: the signature must verify against OUR OWN public key
          # before anything is uploaded.
          openssl rsa -in "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key" -pubout -out pub.pem 2>/dev/null
          openssl dgst -sha256 -verify pub.pem -signature SHA256SUMS.sig SHA256SUMS
          rm -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          # gh-814 r2 trust-anchor drift gate (fail-closed): the public key
          # derived from the secret must equal the PEM embedded in
          # site/install.sh — otherwise every pinned installer would ship an
          # anchor that rejects this release's signed checksums.
          sed -n '/BEGIN PUBLIC KEY/,/END PUBLIC KEY/p' "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/site/install.sh" |
            sed "1s/^.*BEGIN/-----BEGIN/; \$s/END.*\$/END PUBLIC KEY-----/" > embedded-anchor.pem
          openssl pkey -pubin -in embedded-anchor.pem -noout ||
            { echo "::error::site/install.sh trust anchor does not parse as a public key — regenerate installers (dart run scripts/gen_installers.dart)"; exit 1; }
          cmp embedded-anchor.pem pub.pem ||
            { echo "::error::FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY drifted from the trust anchor embedded in site/install.sh — rotate the keypair: update install.signing_public_key in site/install-config.yaml, regenerate installers, and update the repo secret TOGETHER. Refusing to sign (fail-closed)."; exit 1; }
          rm -f pub.pem embedded-anchor.pem

      - name: Upload provenance assets
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          gh release upload "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" \
            provenance/SHA256SUMS provenance/SHA256SUMS.sig \
            --clobber --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"

  # Advance the vpinned release marker to the freshly signed tag. PURE
  # RELEASE-ARTIFACT MANIPULATION — no commits, no pushes: pin_release.sh
  # re-verifies the target's signature itself (fail-closed), then uploads
  # the PINNED_VERSION asset to the standing `vpinned` release. Runs after
  # release-provenance so the signed SHA256SUMS it checks are already
  # published. The marker is only a pointer — installers verify the pointed
  # release's signature against the committed trust anchor, so a tampered
  # marker degrades to a DoS, never a bad binary.
  install-pin-bump:
    name: Advance vpinned marker
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: release-provenance
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # always(): when release-provenance FAILS (e.g. the binaries/signature
    # upload race), plain needs-gating leaves this job SKIPPED — and a
    # `rerun --failed` never resurrects skipped jobs, so the marker stays
    # stale forever (v1.0.483: publish+provenance flaked, the recovery rerun
    # went green, the marker never advanced). With always() the job RUNS
    # even after a failed provenance: pin_release.sh's own pre-move
    # provenance gate (check_install_pin.sh with FA_PIN_TARGET) fails the
    # job loudly instead of moving the marker — and a FAILED job IS part of
    # rerun --failed, so the recovery cascade reaches it.
    if: >-
      always() && github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181…

Quality legs (the "full quality gate"):
1. `changes` (classifier)
2. `cube-kernel-live`
3. `static`
4. `test-core`
5. `integration-mock`
6. `installer-portability`
7. `hostile-env`
8. `fa-aot-build`
9. `pty-integration-linux`
10. `pty-coverage-gate`
11. `pty-visual`
12. `coverage-gate`
13. `guards`
14. `flutter-analyze`
15. `flutter-tests`
16. `flutter-app-exzone`
17. `flutter-app-lock-smoke`
18. `app-crap-gate`
19. `test-faui`

21. `build-web`
22. `build-android`
23. `build-ios`
24. `build-macos`
25. `supply-chain`
26. `dep-audit`
27. `installer-verify`
28. `install-pin-gate`
29. `quality-gate` (aggregate)
30. `perf-gate`, `usage-fold`
31. `step-timings`, `watchdog`

The non-quality legs (tag/release-only): `integration` (provider smoke), `publish`, `binaries`, `web-spa`, `release-provenance`, `install-pin-bump`, `installer-smoke`, `release`, `ci-red-report`.

Now the fix: Add a `release-dedupe` pre-check job that:
- runs only on `github.event_name == 'release'`
- checks whether a CI run for the same tag ref (or head SHA) already exists from the `push` event (`gh run list --branch <tag> --event push`)
- outputs `dedupe=true` if a push run exists (any status) → the release run skips every quality leg and executes only the binaries-attach leg
- outputs `dedupe=false` if not → full gate runs
- fails safe: on API error → `dedupe=false`

Then every quality leg gets `needs: [release-dedupe]` added (careful — they already need `release-pending`) and the `if` gets extended with `&& needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'`.

Also the `quality-gate` aggregate: it needs release-dedupe too, and its own `if: always() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'` needs to become `always() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'`.

Wait — but hold on. If the quality gate is skipped on the release event, then the binaries job `needs: quality-gate` with `if: !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success'` — a skipped quality gate would NOT be 'success', so binaries wouldn't run! That's the fa#456 class of transitive skip. Let me look at that carefully.

The `binaries` job:
```yaml
binaries:
    name: Build native binaries
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 45
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
```

So for the release event with dedupe=true, quality-gate would be skipped (result = 'skipped'), and binaries' `needs.quality-gate.result == 'success'` would be false → binaries skipped. That breaks AC1 — the release run must still execute the binaries-attach leg.

Hmm. But wait — what happens today? Today on the release event, the quality gate runs in full (both push and release runs run the full gate). So `needs.quality-gate.result == 'success'` is satisfiable.

With the dedupe, on the release event with dedupe=true:
- all quality legs skip (dedupe=true)
- quality-gate aggregate: `if: always() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'` — currently the pending output on release events is 'true' (the release-pending job short-circuits to pending=true on non-schedule events). With dedupe, I need to decide: does the aggregate itself skip, or does it run and report skipped legs as pass?

The quality-gate aggregate treats skipped legs as pass ("Skipped legs (path-filtered out) count as pass"). So one option: let the aggregate still RUN on the release-dedupe arm (it would be green, reporting every leg as skipped). That keeps `needs.quality-gate.result == 'success'` true, so binaries/run downstream legs work unchanged. 

But wait — that has a subtlety: the aggregate has the "security legs must EXECUTE and pass" rule:
```
[ "$R_SUPPLY_CHAIN" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="supply-chain = $R_SUPPLY_CHAIN (skipped security is a dodge)"
```
If supply-chain is skipped (dedupe), the aggregate FAILS. So the aggregate needs the dedupe awareness too: when dedupe=true, the security legs' skip is expected, not a dodge.

Hmm, so what to do with the aggregate? Options:

Option A: quality-gate skips too when dedupe=true (`if: always() && pending == 'true' && dedupe != 'true'`), and downstream tag-only jobs (binaries, web-spa, integration...) get updated to handle the skipped aggregate on release events. But `integration` and `publish` are push-only already (`github.event_name == 'push'`), so they're unaffected on release events. `binaries` runs on push OR release. On push, the dedupe output would be... what? On push events, the release-dedupe job must produce `dedupe=false` (a no-op, like release-pending does with pending=true). Actually wait — release-pending outputs `pending=true` by default and only flips to false for empty schedule ticks. For dedupe: the default should be `dedupe=false` (full gate), flipped to true only when (event==release AND push-run-exists). On push/dispatch/schedule events → dedupe=false → quality legs run normally. 

So on push events: dedupe=false → quality-gate runs → binaries works as today.
On release events with dedupe=true: quality legs skip. For binaries to run, either:
  - quality-gate still runs and passes (treating the dedupe skips as expected), or
  - binaries' condition is updated to accept a dedupe-skipped quality-gate.

Option B (cleaner): quality-gate runs on the release-dedupe arm too, but the "Fail on any real failure" step treats the skips as expected when dedupe=true. I.e., pass the dedupe output into the gate step; when dedupe=true, every leg's result should be 'skipped' — if any leg actually RAN (result != skipped), that's suspicious... Actually no: when dedupe=true the legs' ifs evaluate false so they skip. The gate step can then short-circuit: if dedupe=true, verify all legs are skipped (or just pass) and export dart_ok=false (nothing ran, publish shouldn't happen from the release twin anyway — publish is push-only). Hmm, but dart_ok gates publish. On release events publish doesn't run at all (push-only), so dart_ok value on the dedupe arm is moot for publish, but integration also is push-only. So on the dedupe arm: the aggregate can pass with dart_ok=false.

Hmm wait, actually, let me think about what's simplest and safest:

The ticket says: "exists (any status) → output dedupe=true; the release run skips every quality leg (static/test/coverage/guards/flutter) and executes only the binaries-attach leg (idempotent --clobber, last-wins as today). Fast, seconds-to-minutes."

And "Quality legs get needs: [release-dedupe] + if: needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true' (no-op on push/dispatch/schedule events)."

So the design per the ticket: each quality leg gets `needs: [release-dedupe]` (added to their existing needs) and the if extended. The aggregate `quality-gate` — it's the required check. On the release event with dedupe=true: legs skip; aggregate... The ticket says "the release run short-circuits to binaries-attach" — so the aggregate must not block binaries.

Let me think about how binaries can run when quality-gate is skipped. `needs.quality-gate.result == 'success'` fails when skipped. I must update binaries' if. Options:
- `if: !cancelled() && ((needs.quality-gate.result == 'success') || (github.event_name == 'release' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe == 'true')) && (...)` — binaries needs to know the dedupe output, so binaries needs `needs: [release-dedupe, quality-gate]`.

Hmm wait, but there's a subtlety: if quality-gate is skipped and binaries runs on the release event — but the push twin's quality-gate gates the push twin's binaries. The release twin then attaches binaries without a fresh gate. That's exactly the design: the push run (full gate) gates the tag; the release twin just attaches. And AC4: both twins attach binaries with --clobber, last-wins; same commit SHA (the tag), same sources → identical content anyway (modulo build nondeterminism, but --clobber last-wins is the accepted semantics, and it's today's…

There's `test/ci_release_pending_guard_test.dart` — the guard test for the release-pending job (the pattern the ticket says to mirror). Hmm — for the release dedupe, the regression guard could be (a) a Dart workflow-lint test (house pattern for ci.yml guards), or (b) a fixture selftest. The ticket: "A workflow-lint/CI-selftest assertion (aab-gate-selftest pattern) asserting the release-event path short-circuits when a push-run exists for the tag."

blocks.text:
name: AAB 16k gate self-test

# gh-798 AC3: the 16 KB page-size gate (scripts/verify_aab_native_libs.sh,
# called by build-mobile.yml's "Verify AAB" step) is itself tested — a gate
# that is wrong from day one (gh-786: APK-layout glob in an AAB) must be
# caught at PR time, not by the nightly. This job runs the REAL gate script
# against two fixture bundles:
#   (a) libs present (a real 16 KB-aligned vendored .so under the AAB
#       layout base/lib/<abi>/) → gate passes with the green marker;
#   (b) libs absent → the named "::error:: expected native libs …"
#       verdict, never a silent pass, never an inherited exit code.
# A regressed glob or verdict turns this job red and blocks merge — the
# fixture is the AAB layout, so ANY layout assumption regression fails
# case (a) exactly like the nightly did (gh-786). A failure on an
# unrelated change is the desired loudness — fix the gate or fixture,
# never delete the job (gh-798 E3).

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml'
      - '.github/workflows/aab-gate-selftest.yml'
      - 'scripts/verify_aab_native_libs.sh'
      - 'scripts/patch_elf_16k_alignment.dart'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  self-test:
    name: Gate self-test (fixture bundles)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Setup Flutter
        # Only `dart` is needed (the 16 KB checker); flutter-action is the
        # repo-standard pinned source of it and mirrors the real leg.
        uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: 'stable'
          cache: true

      - name: Build fixture bundles (AAB layout, with/without native libs)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # (a) with libs: a REAL 16 KB-aligned .so from the vendored
          # wasm_run plugin, packaged at the AAB layout.
          mkdir -p fx/with-libs/base/lib/arm64-v8a
          cp vendor/wasm_run_flutter/android/src/main/jniLibs/arm64-v8a/libwasm_run_dart.so fx/with-libs/base/lib/arm64-v8a/
          (cd fx/with-libs && zip -q -r -X ../with-libs.aab base)
          # (b) without libs: structurally valid bundle, zero native libs.
          mkdir -p fx/without-libs/base
          (cd fx/without-libs && zip -q -r -X ../without-libs.aab base)
          unzip -l fx/with-libs.aab 'base/lib/*'

      - name: "(a) libs present → gate passes"
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          OUT="$(mktemp)"
          if bash scripts/verify_aab_native_libs.sh fx/with-libs.aab >"$OUT" 2>&1; then
            cat "$OUT"
          else
            echo "::error::gate must PASS on a bundle WITH native libs (gh-798 AC3a) — regressed glob or layout assumption?"
            cat "$OUT"
            exit 1
          fi
          grep -q "✅ 16 KB alignment check green" "$OUT" || {
            echo "::error::gate passed without its green marker — verdict text drifted (gh-798 AC3a)"
            exit 1
          }

      - name: "(b) libs absent → named failure, never a silent pass"
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          OUT="$(mktemp)"
          if bash scripts/verify_aab_native_libs.sh fx/without-libs.aab >"$OUT" 2>&1; then
            echo "::error::gate must FAIL on a bundle WITHOUT native libs (gh-798 AC3b) — native libs are expected in the store bundle"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Replay the output as PROOF of the named verdict — but strip the
          # ::error:: command marker first, so the EXPECTED failure does not
          # paint a red annotation onto this (green) run (gh-800 r2).

# merge guard (sm_merge_guard.py), gh-1568.

#   AC1 (the gh-1568 regression) a merge-commit landing whose tree equals
#       a successful dispatch's commit tree VALIDATES — with the commits
#       API served in its REAL shape (tree nested under `commit`, no
#       top-level `tree` key). The shipped `.tree.sha` jq path resolved
#       empty for every run, so every merge-commit landing false-alarmed
#       (issue #1568: merges 392fe540ae of #1484 and afed64bfd0 of #1468
#       both carried trees byte-identical to their green validations).
#   AC2 an UNCOVERED tree still alarms (exit 3) — the fix must not mute
#       the invariant.
#   AC3 a fast-forward landing (pushed sha == validated head sha)
#       validates with no tree lookup at all.
#   AC4 the race: a validation still in_progress at push time can never
#       certify — alarm (the SM merges strictly after green, so
#       in_progress-at-push means the merge beat the validation).
#   AC5 a failed tree lookup (commit API 404) degrades to a warning and
#       alarms — never a false validate, never a traceback.
#   AC6 the alarm body renders each considered run's resolved tree, so
#       future alarms are self-diagnosing, and files with the
#       bug+sm-guard labels (dedup convention untouched).
# Same discipline as check_lockfiles_selftest.sh (#1100 pattern).
set -u
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
GUARD="$HERE/sm_merge_guard.py"
TMP="$(mktemp -d)"
trap '[ "${KEEP:-0}" = 1 ] || rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

fails=0
check() { # check <desc> <condition-exit-code: 0 = pass>
  if [ "$2" = "0" ]; then
    echo "  ok: $1"

    fails=$((fails + 1))

}

{"content":"#!/usr/bin/env bash
